(OpenPnP's Primary calibration fiducial position and initial camera calibration; jog the camera over the primary fiducial; Accept calibrates the camera there and makes the fiducial it finds, its place and diameter, the primary fiducial: a new machine's first vision step, as nothing else is known yet); a head without visual homing (Accept finds the round mark under its camera, makes it the homing mark, its place and width, and turns visual homing on: jog the camera over it first), the calibration rig's two fiducials less than 2 mm apart in Z, and the head's first nozzle's Safe Z not above a rig fiducial. As OpenPnP's CameraSolutions: a Preview FPS over 15 (Accept sets 5), a preview not suspended during tasks (an error for a switcher camera; Accept suspends it), Auto Camera View off (Accept turns it on), and Rendering Quality Low (Accept sets High). And, as OpenPnP's, a capture device's own settings (read from it as it starts): brightness, contrast, gamma, gain, hue, saturation and white balance at their defaults and not automatic, sharpness at its minimum (Accept sets each by hand so), and exposure not automatic (Accept keeps the value it has chosen, set by hand: have it look at a representative, rather bright subject). As OpenPnP's VisionSolutions (in plainer words; what was solved there stays solved), once the calibration rig's primary fiducial X and Y is known: Set nozzle N approximate offsets and capture the primary fiducial height (coarse nozzle calibration). for the head's first nozzle, and Set nozzle N approximate offsets and match its Z to nozzle F (coarse nozzle calibration)., F the first nozzle, for each other nozzle, once the fiducial's height is known: jog the nozzle down until its tip touches the primary fiducial and Accept. The nozzle's X and Y offsets from the camera are the fiducial's position less where its axes are (X and Y already within half the fiducial of these are kept, as they may already be precise). The first nozzle becomes the reference in Z (its Z offset 0) and the height it touches is kept as the fiducial's; another nozzle's Z offset is set so it reads the same Z there. Set the secondary fiducial height (probed with nozzle N)., for the first nozzle only, once the secondary fiducial's X and Y is known: its tip touching the secondary fiducial gives that fiducial's height, the camera's second scale; no nozzle offsets change. Each is refused above Safe Z, or with the two fiducials' heights less than 2 mm apart; Undo puts them back. Calibration A nozzle tip that no nozzle takes. As OpenPnP's CalibrationSolutions: each head's X and Y backlash, once its camera is calibrated and its homing mark set (Accept measures it with the camera over the mark, and keeps what it finds). Work on the machine that cannot start makes Accept fail, saying why; as OpenPnP's, an issue whose work starts stays open while it runs and is Solved only once it has succeeded (failing, it stays open: Accept tries again). A nozzle tip without a background calibration method: chosen in the issue (Brightness and Key-Color, or Brightness), then Accept calibrates the tip on the nozzle it is loaded on. As OpenPnP's CalibrationSolutions, for each nozzle with its offsets roughly set: Calibrate nozzle N's precise offsets from the camera (fine nozzle calibration). (OpenPnP's Calibrate precise camera ↔ nozzle N offsets.) Place the test object on the primary fiducial and target it with the head camera; Test Object Diameter (mm: the rig's Test Object, as the nozzle's Calibration tab shows it; looked for in pixels by the camera's scale, 20 px when it is not known): each change is kept as the rig's and finds a round feature of that size near the picture's middle and shows it on the camera's view (the green circle and cross-hairs that should hug the object, "Diameter N px - Score S"); Auto-Detect Next tries every size and takes (and keeps, in mm) the next one bigger, where a round feature is found, that scores best among its neighbours (pressed again, the next; a size where nothing is found counts for nothing, as in OpenPnP, so it does not stop on the picture's noise); Test Object Thickness: the rig's test object's top above the primary fiducial it lies on, typed in or set by Capture Test Object Thickness, the nozzle's Z with its tip touching the object less the fiducial's (0: paper-thin). Accept, at the Test Object Diameter as set (not measured again), looks for it on the primary fiducial, then the nozzle picks it at six angles round the circle and places it turned 180 degrees, the camera finding it after each (with the head's two heights, again on the secondary fiducial, the nozzle carrying it there and back: the nozzle's lean, as the nozzle's Calibration tab says) (as OpenPnP's: three times over, by the same round-feature search as the Test Object Diameter's, at the test object's diameter and no more than a tenth bigger or smaller, so a test object with an inner ring is found by the ring of its size; each picture shown on the camera, "Nozzle Offset Calibration N° - Score S"); the offsets change by the average of where it moved (the true axis midway; runout cancels out), with what depends on them; each angle's own estimate is in the log, and the result says how far, at most, any of them is from the average: how much the result can be trusted (estimates far apart: the object slipping, a tip that is worn or loose, the camera not settling); the correction is shown at once, in a dialog ("Nozzle offsets calibrated": how far the offsets moved in X and Y and in all, then the detected and the previous offsets), and the result (detected, previous, difference) is shown with the issue whenever it is looked at again (Include Solved?). Production The tables not linked between tabs (Accept sets View > Selections in Tables to Linked), as OpenPnP's VisionSolutions. Advanced G-code not compressed, comments not removed (Accept turns each on); before Advanced, the other way, offered only (never counted as open). Script engines not pooled (Accept ticks the machine's Pool scripting engines?). any A Photon feeder's slot without a location, or without an offset from it.

Choosing an issue selects its part in Machine Setup, ready there when you open that tab.

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text:
jplacer keeps jobs, boards and panels in files of its own: a job is a .jpjob, a board a .jpboard and a panel a .jppanel. OpenPnP's .job.xml, .board.xml and .panel.xml are read as they are, so a job, board or panel made in OpenPnP opens in jplacer; saved, each is written as jplacer's file beside OpenPnP's, which is left as it was.

  • A job (.jpjob; OpenPnP's .job.xml is read) holds the boards and panels to be placed, each where it lies on the machine and which side is up, and what the job sets on them: which placements are placed, which boards and placements are enabled, whether each board's fiducials are checked, and how each placement's errors are handled.
  • A board (.jpboard; OpenPnP's .board.xml is read) holds its placements (designator, side, location, rotation, part, type, comments, error handling, enabled), its parts list, each pointing at a library part (see Boards), its dimensions and outline, and its solder paste pads. A board can be used many times, in one job or several; each use shares the board's file.
  • A panel (.jppanel; OpenPnP's .panel.xml is read) holds boards and other panels, each where it lies on the panel, the panel's own fiducials, and pseudo-placements: a placement of one of its boards (a fiducial, say) used to line up the whole panel.
  • The library's parts and packages, the only ones there are, are kept in library.db (see Parts), in jplacer's configuration folder (~/.config/jplacer). The boards and panels open are the job's (see Boards). A part has an id, a name, a height (and the depth it reaches through the board), a package, a speed and how many times a pick is tried again. A package has an id, a description, a tape specification, vacuum levels, a footprint (its pads and body), the nozzle tips that can pick it, and its vision settings. Parts and packages are found by id whatever its case.

The job is edited on the Job tab (below), panels, boards, parts and packages on the Panels, Boards, Parts and Packages tabs, as in OpenPnP.

docs.title: New, open and save
docs.text:
Entry File ▸ New Job (Ctrl+N) Starts an empty job. File ▸ Open Job… (Ctrl+O) Opens a .jpjob file, or OpenPnP's .job.xml. File ▸ Save Job (Ctrl+S) Saves the job to its file; a job never saved asks where, as Save Job As does. File ▸ Save Job As… Saves the job to a file you choose (the file chooser starts at the job's own file); .jpjob is added if you leave it off.

A job opened from OpenPnP's .job.xml is saved beside it as jplacer's file, under its own name (sim.job.xml becomes sim.jpjob, a number added if that name is taken; the status bar says Saved as jplacer's …), and from then on the job is that file. The .job.xml is left exactly as it was.

The window's title is jplacer - * and the job's file name (Untitled.jpjob for a job never saved), with a * before the name while it has changes that are not saved. The job you had open is opened again, with its boards and panels, the next time jplacer starts, when Machine Setup's Auto-load most recent job?* is ticked.

If the job has unsaved changes when you start another job, open one, or close jplacer, you are asked Do you want to save your changes? Yes saves them first (asking where, for a job never saved), No lets them go, Cancel leaves things as they were. Then each of its boards and panels with changes is asked about the same way, as they close with the job. File ▸ Open Recent Job... offers the ten jobs opened or saved last. Saving over a file that is there asks first whether to replace it.

A job's boards and panels are found by their file names: as written in the job, else beside the panel that holds them, else beside the job.

docs.title: Older OpenPnP jobs
docs.text: A job saved by an older OpenPnP (a list of boards, perhaps one panel of rows and columns of one board) is converted when it is opened, as OpenPnP converts it: a panel of rows and columns becomes a panel file of its own (name.jppanel, beside the job), its boards named Brd[row,column]; what was placed is kept. The job is then marked as changed, so saving it writes it as jplacer's .jpjob (the old file is left as it was).

docs.title: The Job tab
docs.text:
The Job tab (the first in the work area, as in OpenPnP) shows the job's boards and panels and, under them the chosen one: a board's Placements, with its imports, revisions, parts and viewer (see Boards); or a panel's definition, its children and fiducials (see Panels). There is no other place a board or panel is kept: each is the job's.

Boards: every board and panel in the job, those on a panel under it and indented, with a board or panel mark: Board/Panel Id, Name (pointing at it shows the file), Width, Length, Side, X, Y, Z, Rot., Enabled? and Check Fids?. Where one lies is shown on green once a fiducial check has set it on the machine, on blue when set on its panel. Those straight in the job are changed in the table; one on a panel can only be turned on or off and have its fiducial check changed. A board's or panel's Name, Width and Length are its own, changed wherever it is. Right-click for Set Side, Set Enabled and Set Check Fids.

Button Start (Pause, Resume), Step, Stop Run the job (see Running the job). Alert Errors / Defer Errors Whether a placement's error (one whose error handling is Default) stops the job at once, or is reported at its end. Click to change. Add Board/Panel (plus, with a menu) New Board..., Existing Board..., New Panel..., Existing Panel..., and Copy of the Chosen Board... (or Panel...: a copy saved as a new file): put one in the job, at the machine's Default Board Location (Machine Setup). Remove Board(s)/Panel(s) (cross) Takes the chosen ones (straight in the job) out of it. Move Camera To Board Location, Move Camera to the Next Board, Move Tool To Board Location Take the camera (or the Jog panel's nozzle) to where the board lies, at safe Z; Next chooses the next row first. Capture Camera Location Sets where the chosen board lies to where the camera is (its X, Y and rotation; its Z kept). Capture Tool Location Sets the chosen boards' Z to the nozzle's. Fiducial Check Looks at the chosen board's (or panel's) fiducials with the camera and sets where it lies from them, as the job does; one straight in the job has its X, Y and rotation set too (and its Z, measured, with the Fiducial Locator's Measure Board Z?, as a job's check sets it). The camera is then taken to it. Each fiducial looked for has its package's footprint drawn over the cameras (as a job's check does too), the last chosen footprint until another is. Board Nudge (a toggle, lit when on) Moves the chosen board's X and Y by what you jog the camera while it is on, to line a part up by eye when a fiducial check is a little out (below). Measure Board Z (a toggle, lit when on) Machine Setup's Fiducial Locator Measure Board Z?, turned on or off from here: with it on, a fiducial check (this one and a job's) measures the board's height at each of its fiducials and sets its Z from their mean. Pressed, only that setting is changed (and saved with the machine's setup, Machine Setup showing it); press it again to take it back. It follows a change made in Machine Setup. Multiple Point Board Location Sets where the chosen board lies from placements you jog the camera over (below). Photograph Board (camera) Photographs the chosen boards (a panel's: every board on it) with the head camera, one after another; Stop stops it (see Board photos). View Job Opens the job viewer (see Panels), following the boards chosen.

Placements: the chosen board's (or panel's) placements on its side facing up, with Placed and Status (Ready, Missing Part, Missing Feeder, Part Height: its height is not known, or Disabled). A board's own (its placements' IDs, parts, sides, where they lie, types, comments) are changed here, for every use of it (and New and Remove Placement(s) work: the board's parts that no placement uses after a removal go with them, so the next import of those parts starts from the library as it is); Enabled, Placed and Error Handling for this use alone. Move Camera To Placement Location, Move Tool To Placement Location, Capture Camera Placement Location and Capture Tool Placement Location work as the board ones, for the chosen placement. Move Camera To Previous Placement Location and To Next (the arrows either side of it) choose the placement before or after the chosen one, as the table shows them (none chosen: the last, or the first), and take the camera there. Edit Placement Feeder (one placement of a board) opens the Feeders tab on the feeder holding its part: an enabled one first, else a disabled one, else a new feeder is made for it. Right-click for Set Type, Set Side, Set Placed, Set Enabled and Set Error Handling; Space turns the chosen placement on or off.

A placement whose part is not in the library shows in Part what the files called it: its part's name (else its value and footprint) and (to be chosen), or (not in the library) when its library part was deleted. What the files said is kept with the board, whatever happens in the library; point at the cell for all of it, and click it to choose the part again.

Columns also offers each placement's part's columns and its part's package's, headed Part ▸ and Package ▸ (Part ▸ Value, Part ▸ MPN, Package ▸ Name…, the fields you added to parts and packages too), hidden until you tick them. They are the Parts and Packages tabs' own and are changed here as there: the library's part (or package) is changed, so every placement of it shows the change, and the status line says how many placements here are of it. Edit ▸ Undo takes it back as a change to the library. A placement with no part shows nothing there.

docs.title: Verifying placements
docs.text:
The chosen placement's footprint (a fiducial's too) is drawn over the cameras' pictures: its part's package's footprint, its pads and pin 1's mark, not its body, as OpenPnP's package reticle. The cameras show one footprint, the last chosen, here or on the Packages tab (or chosen there by View ▸ Selections in Tables ▸ Linked); it stays when another tab is shown. On a camera with a rotation axis it is turned by the camera's rotation, as that is now: take the camera to the placement (Move Camera To Placement Location), which turns the camera to the placement's rotation whatever tool Jog has, and look: the footprint should lie on the board's pads, turned as the part will be placed.

  • Turn 90° turns the chosen placement a quarter counter-clockwise: a correction to the CAD file's rotation (which the placement keeps apart, as it came). Take the camera to it again to see it turned.
  • Verified, Next marks the chosen placement verified and takes the camera to the next one shown, facing up, not verified yet.

The Verified column says whether each was, and when (Yes, Position only). Changing a placement's position, rotation or part takes its mark off: what was checked is no longer what is placed.

Importing from the CPL and BOM turns a placement by its footprint's Zero Rotation (see Packages), where the library's footprint for its part has one: CAD tools disagree about which way 0° faces. The CAD file's rotation is kept with it.

The status line shows the placements placed: of the whole job, and of the board chosen.

Multiple Point Board Location shows its steps across the top of the Job tab, with Cancel and Next: choose two or more placements of the board (four, near its corners, is better) and click Next; the camera goes near the first; jog its crosshairs over the placement's centre and click Next, and so on for each (the shortest way round). The board is then fitted to them as a fiducial check fits it, and refused if it scales or shears more than 5 % or moves more than 5 mm. Finish takes the camera to the board's origin; Cancel puts the board back where it was.

Board Nudge is for when every part comes out the same few hundredths of a millimetre off after a fiducial check. Take the camera to a placement (Move Camera To Placement Location), turn Board Nudge on, and jog the camera until its crosshairs are on the part. Across the top of the Job tab it says how far you have jogged, as you jog; Apply (or turning Board Nudge off) moves the board's X and Y by that much, so every placement follows, and Cancel leaves the board where it was. The board's rotation and Z stay as they are. Any move other than jogging (to another placement or board, Multiple Point Board Location, another board chosen) ends it without moving the board, as does the machine going. It nudges a board straight in the job, not one inside a panel. The next fiducial check sets the board's location again, as ever. It is not an Edit ▸ Undo step: to take one back, nudge the other way.

docs.title: Shortages
docs.text:
Job ▸ Shortages… sets the job's parts against the stock, the parts shortest of stock first. Each row gives the Part, how many placements are Left to place (enabled, on the side facing up, not placed yet), the Attrition allowed (how many more, at the part's own share, or the share its ledger measured, or not known), how many are In stock in its open lots, how many it is Short, its Lots (each with where it is kept and what it holds) and, when short, where it is bought (Buy from: the part's offers). A part not chosen yet keeps no stock, and says so. The line at the top counts the placements, the parts and those short.

Stock never stops a run: the feeders hold what is placed, and a part can be loaded as the run reaches it.

docs.title: Running the job
docs.text:
Start runs the job, a step after another, until every placement is placed; while it runs the button is Pause, which stops it after the step under way, and then Resume. Step does one step (on to the next that moves the machine, with Machine Setup's Step Next Motion) and pauses. Stop stops it: the nozzles are emptied at the discard location and the head is parked (so too when the step under way at the time fails: the status line then says how). The machine must be connected (the buttons are greyed until it is) and homed. A run paused when the machine's connection is lost is ended with Stop, which stays available: nothing moves, and the status line says "Job stopped without the machine: its nozzles not emptied." (take off by hand anything left on them). Quitting while a job runs or is paused stops it the same way first, then quits. If every placement is placed already, Start asks whether to mark them all not placed first. The status line says what the job is doing ("Feed …", "Pick … using nozzle N1.", "Placing …"), and at the end how many parts were placed and how fast. While a job runs, another job or another cell is not opened. While the machine is busy with a task of its own (a Test Alignment, a feeder's or a fiducial check's moves, a Recycle), Start, Step, Stop and another such task are refused: the status line says "The machine is busy with a task: wait for it to finish", and the click does nothing (OpenPnP queues it instead). Start, Step and Stop are also in the toolbar at the top of the window, after the machine's power and home buttons, so a job can be run from any tab: they are the Job tab's, greyed and turned to Pause or Resume as those are.

Checking the job. Before a run starts (and with Job ▸ Check Job… at any time), the job's data is checked as one list, each thing once with every placement or part it is about (a placement named by its board's ID and its own, Brd1⇒R1), and where it is put right. Only the placements a run places are looked at: enabled, not placed, their side up on an enabled board.

  • Stop: the run would refuse it: a placement ID used twice on a board; No part chosen (the board's part is still to be chosen); a part the library does not have; a part with No package; No nozzle tip on the machine fits its package.
  • Check: worth putting right first: placements Not verified on the machine (see Verifying placements), parts whose Height is not known, parts with No footprint to draw or check against.
  • Note: parts No feeder holds yet (the run asks for them, see Load as you go); parts Short of stock, of those whose stock is kept (a part with no lots at all is not).

Start with nothing to stop or check runs at once, and so does Start with only things to check or note when Preferences' Check the job before each run is unticked. Otherwise Check Job shows the list: with anything that stops the run it is not started (Close); with only things to check or note, Start Anyway runs it as it is and Cancel does not. Choose a row to see under the list all it is about (the first 60). The counts at the top say how many are to put right, to check and to note.

A job goes as OpenPnP's does:

  1. Checks. The placements to place are those enabled, not placed, with their side facing up on an enabled board. Each must have a part, the part a package, and a nozzle tip that fits the package and a nozzle; a board with an ID twice is refused. A part no feeder holds is not refused: it is asked for when the run gets to it (see Load as you go). Then the head goes to safe Z and anything left on a nozzle is discarded.
  2. Fiducials. Each board and panel with Check Fids? has its fiducials found by the camera (a panel's outermost first), each as a round mark the size of its package's footprint pad, looked at again once centred as its Fiducial Vision Settings say (by default up to three times, until a look moves it less than 0.2 mm; from either side with a parallax diameter). Where the board lies is fitted to them: with two, moved, turned and scaled; with three or more, fully. A fit that scales or shears more than 5 %, or moves the board more than 5 mm, is refused.
  3. Planning. The placements still to do, lowest rank first (a rank ten or more above the lowest waits for it), are ordered as Machine Setup's Job order says (by nozzle tip unless set otherwise, see Job Processors); each nozzle is given one, with the tip on it if one fits, else a tip that does. A nozzle after the first takes, of those its tip fits, the one quickest for the head to reach from the middle of the picks and the middle of the places already planned (as OpenPnP's planner: the time the head's X and Y axes take, from their speed and acceleration, to where the head goes for that nozzle); with two nozzles, the other way round where that is quicker.

  4. Each cycle: the nozzle tips changed where needed (by their changer steps), the nozzles turned for the pick, each part fed (retried as the feeder's Feed Retry Count says; an empty feeder is turned off and the next one holding the part used) and picked (retried as its Pick Retry Count says, a part that was not picked discarded), then placed where the board lies, as high as the part, turned to the placement's rotation. Then the next cycle, until all are placed; then the head is parked.

  5. Alignment (bottom vision), when the machine's bottom vision is on and the part's Bottom Vision Settings are enabled: the nozzle takes the part over the camera looking up, its bottom at the camera's focus, turned to the placement's angle (pre-rotated, as the settings' Pre-rotate and the machine say; else at 0°), as OpenPnP's bottom vision does. The part is found by its settings' pipeline, as OpenPnP finds it, turned less than 45° either way of the angle wanted (all the way round with Rotation: Full). Pre-rotated, the nozzle is moved and turned by what was seen and the part looked at again, until it is off by less than the machine's Max. Linear Offset (its corner too, as turned) and Max. Angular Offset, or the machine's passes run out. The settings' Vision Center Offsets are taken off what was found; offsets further than the nozzle tip's Max. Pick Tolerance fail it ("Part R1 bottom vision offsets length 0.713mm larger than the allowed Max. Pick Tolerance 0.500mm set on nozzle tip NT1."), as does the Part size check. Each look is tried again up to Max Vision Attempts. The part is then placed with what was found taken off: the nozzle turned by what the part is off, and moved by its offset on the nozzle. A part with bottom vision off is placed as it was picked.

When something fails, the job pauses and says why (Job Error); the board, placement, part or feeder it is about is chosen on its tab. Resume goes on from there. A part taken off its nozzle while the job is paused (the Jog panel's Discard, after bottom vision could not find it, say) is fed and picked again for its placement when the job goes on, rather than looked for on the nozzle. With Defer Errors (or a placement's own error handling set to Defer), a placement that fails is put off instead: its feeder's fault is counted (shown in the Feeders tab's Faults; by default three in its last six feeds turn the feeder off), and it is tried again later, up to Machine Setup's Max Placement Attempts, or left in error; the job goes on, and says at its end how many errors there were.

Deleting during a run. A placement deleted while the job runs or is paused (or a board taken out of the job) is left out of the run from the next step. If its part is already on a nozzle, the part is dropped at the discard location; if not, it is never picked. The status line says which ("D13 deleted from the job: its part on nozzle RIGHT discarded.", "R5 deleted from the job: not placed."). The rest of the run goes on, and the placements left out are not counted as errors at its end.

docs.title: The plan
docs.text:
Job ▸ Plan… shows the job's placements left to place in groups of one part each, in the order a run places them: #, the Part, how many are Left, its Height, its Package, and where it Comes from (the feeder holding it, or a load the run will ask for). The line at the top counts the parts, the placements and the loads.

Order by chooses the order:

  • Machine's job order (as a job starts): the run orders the placements as Machine Setup's Job Order says, as OpenPnP does; the groups are listed by name.
  • Height: the lowest parts first, so tall ones are not in the nozzle's way; then the smallest package.
  • Package size: the smallest package body first; then the lowest.
  • Most first: the groups with the most placements first.
  • Name.

Move Up and Move Down move the chosen group: groups moved by hand come first, in their order, and the rest follow as sorted. Sort Again drops the order set by hand, and choosing another order sorts them all again. With an order chosen or a group moved, the run places group by group: the Job Order applies within a group, and a nozzle is given a placement of the next group only when the groups before it have none left for it. The plan is kept in the job's file.

docs.title: Load as you go
docs.text:
A part does not have to be on a feeder for a job to start. The run places every part that is loaded first; when only parts no feeder holds are left, it pauses and asks for the next one: in the plan's order (see The plan), or with no plan the lowest first (tall parts last, out of the nozzle's way), then by name. Load part says what to load, how it comes (the part's first packaging: its tape, pitch and how the part is turned in it), and into which Lane: a lane is a strip feeder, laid by hand. The lanes offered are those free for it, best first: an empty one (no part, or turned off), then one whose part this run no longer needs (said, so it is taken off first); of each, those of the part's tape width first, and one of another width says so. A lane holding a part the run still needs is never offered. Where the part's stock is kept, Lot chooses which of its lots is being loaded (the only one is chosen already).

  • Continue: lay the strip as the lane's strips lie, its first part at the lane's first hole. The lane is set to the part, turned on, its feed count started again (and the holes its vision found forgotten), the chosen lot loaded on it (the lot there before taken off), and the run goes on.
  • Skip This Part: its placements are left unplaced, in error ("Skipped: not loaded"), and the run goes on; the end of the run counts them with the errors and the log names each.
  • Stop stops the run. Escape and the [x] leave it paused: Resume asks again.

With no lane free, the prompt says so: set a feeder up for the part on the Feeders tab, then Continue; or skip it.

docs.title: Board photos
docs.text:
A board's photo is one picture of it made from many taken with the head camera: a record of the bare board, or of what was placed and where. The Job tab's Photograph Board takes one of each board chosen (the machine connected and homed, the job stopped), the status line saying how far it has got ("Photographing Brd1: picture 10 of 49"); Stop stops it, and nothing is kept of the board under way. With the Job Processor's Photograph boards as the job starts? or …as the job ends? ticked (Machine Setup), the job takes them too: each enabled board once its fiducials are checked, before a part is placed, and once every placement is done, before the head parks; a picture a step, so Pause, Step and Stop work between them. A photo that cannot be taken is said in the status line and the log, and the job goes on.

The pictures cover the board's outline and 1 mm round it (a board with no size: its placements and 2 mm round them), a quarter of each overlapping the next, row by row from the top, each row the other way from the last, at the height of the board's surface; a picture out of the camera's reach is left out. Each is put where the machine says it was taken, then lined up with its neighbours by what they both show, and they are blended across their overlaps. The photo is at the camera's own scale, coarser where that would make it more than 25 million pixels, square to the board whatever its angle on the machine. A board needs its file saved first: its photos are kept beside it, in a folder of its name and .photos (grblhal.jpboard.photos), each a PNG named by when it was taken, the board's id in the job and why (2026-10-12 14-42-45 Brd1 jobEnd.png), with what it is beside it (its scale, where it lies on the board, the job and run). Every photo is kept until you delete it.

What is said of a photo (in the log, and under it in the Board Viewer): a picture moved more than 0.1 mm to line up with its neighbours (the camera was that far from where the machine said: check the head camera's calibration and the axes' backlash compensation); neighbours still disagreeing by more than 0.05 mm once lined up (the lens not fully straightened, or the board moved); overlaps too plain to line up by (the bare spaces between boards: those pictures stay where the machine put them); pictures out of reach, and the share of the board's area not in the photo (shown clear).

docs.title: Runs
docs.text:
Each Start of a job begins a run, recorded as it goes in runs.db beside the library: when it started, the job, its boards at their revisions, each part fed (from which feeder, and the stock lot the feeder carries) and each placement placed. So a run cut short (jplacer closed, or the computer stopped) still says what it used.

When the run ends (finished, or stopped with Stop), its parts are written to the stock's ledger, one entry of each for every lot its feeders carried: those placed as Used, those fed and not placed (mis-picked, dropped, discarded) as Lost, each with the run as its reference. A run left open is written when jplacer next opens, ended as Interrupted. A run paused by an error stays open until it is resumed and ends, or is stopped.

While a run goes, after each feed from a feeder carrying a lot, if the lot holds fewer by its count than the run still has to place of the part, the status line and the log say so once: "Upper Strips - 1: reel A has about 15 left by its count, and 40 of C0603-100n are still to place".

Job ▸ Runs… lists the newest 200 runs: Started, Ended, How it ended (Finished, Stopped, Interrupted, or Open while it runs), the Job, the Boards (each with its revision), how many were Placed, and whether its parts are in the Ledger yet.

docs.title: Log
docs.text:
The Log tab shows what jplacer's log says as it says it, as OpenPnP's Log tab does: one line an entry, its time, where it comes from, its level and what it says ("2026-10-05 12:00:00.123 job INFO: Job finished without error"), coloured by its level in the theme's colours, readable on its background (information and debug in the text's own colour, trace dimmed, warnings in the warning colour, errors in the danger colour; OpenPnP's blue and its errors' pale band are for its white background). While the list is at its end it follows the newest entry.

The log is also written to a file as it comes, as OpenPnP's log/OpenPnP.log: log/jplacer.log in jplacer's folder (~/.config/jplacer), each entry a line as the tab shows it. Past 10 MB it is moved aside to jplacer.log.1 (the one before that dropped) and begun again. Help > Submit Diagnostics can include it.

Global Logging Settings ▸ Global Log Level sets how much the log says at all: it is the log's own level, the same as the Console's Log, and kept for next time.

Filter Logging Panel chooses what is shown of it, not what is logged; its Search, Log Level and System Output are kept for next time:

Search Only entries with this text in them, whatever its case; its ✕ empties it. Log Level Only entries of this level and above. System Output Entries from the framework and libraries jplacer uses, as well as jplacer's own. Clear log (✕) The entries taken away. Copy to clipboard The entries shown, copied as text. Scroll down The newest entry brought into view.

Ctrl+C copies the entries chosen in the list.

docs.title: Machine Setup
docs.text: Machine Setup (Machine > Machine Setup…, or its tab in the work area) is where the machine is described: what it is made of, and how each part is set up. A machine brought in from OpenPnP arrives set up; here it is looked at, changed and added to.

docs.title: The tree
docs.text:
The machine is shown as a tree of its parts, in OpenPnP's order, each named as OpenPnP names it, its class and then its name (ReferenceHead H1, GcodeAsyncDriver Jaytek), with OpenPnP's icon before a nozzle, a camera, a driver and an axis (linear or rotation):

  • Axes: every axis, whichever controller drives it.
  • Signalers: what tells you how a job is going (below).
  • Feeders: every feeder, with OpenPnP's feeder icon: choosing one shows its page as the Feeders tab has it (and chooses it there), its settings and buttons the same.
  • Heads: each head, and on it its Nozzles, Cameras and Actuators.
  • Nozzle Tips: the tips the nozzles take, each with its Load and Unload steps under it.
  • Cameras: the cameras fixed to the machine (looking up at the nozzles).
  • Actuators: the actuators on the machine rather than a head.
  • Drivers: the controllers the machine is wired to.
  • Job Processors: ReferencePnpJobProcessor, how a job is run (below).
  • Vision: Bottom Vision and Fiducal Locator (OpenPnP's spelling), how parts and fiducials are found (below).

Choose a part to see its settings beside the tree, each the full height of the panel; drag the divider between them to give either more room (where it is is kept for next time). Over the tree, OpenPnP's Expand opens every branch when ticked and closes them when not, and Search keeps to the rows whose name contains what is typed (and the groups they are in), with everything under them, and to the rows whose page has a setting, tab or group of that name ("motion": the controller's Motion Control Type, the machine's Motion Planner); chosen, such a page opens on the tab that has it. The × at its right clears it. Right-click a row for Open This Branch and Close This Branch (the row and everything under it), Open All, Close All (down to the machine's groups), and New and Delete as the tools above. A line under the settings says what the last change could not do, or what is not in use until put right, only while there is something to say. Every change is put in use and saved at once, as OpenPnP's Apply does, even one that makes something wrong (an axis set to no controller, say): the problem is said in a dialog when it starts (with the change that made it), listed under the settings and in Issues & Solutions, and refused where it is used (Home, or a move on that axis, says why). Only a setup that could not even be read back (a transformed axis still without its input, part way through being made) waits, said in a dialog at once, with every change after it. A camera's gear icon (in its tab) opens Machine Setup on that camera.

docs.title: Job Processors
docs.text:
ReferencePnpJobProcessor holds OpenPnP's settings for running a job (imported from an OpenPnP machine):

Setting Max Placement Attempts How many times a placement is tried, when its errors are deferred, before it is left in error. Job order How the placements are ordered: Part, Height:Part, Part:Board, Height:Part:Board, Board:Part, Pick Locations, Pick and Place Locations (the shortest way between feeders, then between places: found, as every route a job takes, by OpenPnP's travelling salesman, its simulated annealing seeded as OpenPnP's so the same job gives the same route, a hop costed by the time the default head camera's X and Y axes take at their feed rates and accelerations), Nozzle Tips (the default: by the tip that picks them, the busiest first), Nozzle Tips (Inflexible Tips First) or Unsorted. A placement the tips already on the nozzles can pick still goes first. Nozzle tip loading strategy Minimize tip changes; Start As Planned, the first cycle of a job as the order says, then as Minimize; Fully As Planned, always as the order says. Max Vision Attempts How many times a part's vision alignment is tried. Step Next Motion Step runs on to the next step that moves the machine. Optimize Multiple Nozzles With several nozzles, picks and places in the shortest way rather than in nozzle order. Pre-Rotate All Nozzles Turns every nozzle for its pick (and its place) on the way: as OpenPnP's, not a move of its own, the turn goes with the next move made with every Z on the head in its safe zone (both nozzles turned for their placements as the head sets off for the first). Feeder fault limit, Feeder fault window size With deferred errors, a feeder is turned off when this many of its last so many feeds and picks failed. Photograph boards as the job starts?, Photograph boards as the job ends? (Board Photos) Each board the job places photographed with the head camera once its fiducials are checked, before a part is placed, and once every placement is done, before the head parks (see Board photos). Off to begin with.

The fiducial check's tolerances (5 % scale, 5 % shear, 5 mm of movement) and how many levels of panels are checked first are taken from an imported OpenPnP machine too.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text:
Bottom Vision holds OpenPnP's ReferenceBottomVision settings: Enabled? (parts are aligned over the camera looking up), Bottom Vision Settings (the machine's default, for parts and packages that name none), Rotate parts prior to vision?, Max. vision passes, Max. linear offset (mm) and Max. angular offset (degrees): a part off by less than both after a pass is taken as found. Its offset is applied when it is placed (the nozzle goes to the placement less it); it is not looked at again. Further than either, the nozzle moves so the part is centred and turned as wanted, and it is looked at again, up to Max. vision passes looks, the last one taken whatever it shows. The first look comes in by way of Safe Z; the ones after it, the nozzle already within the camera's Roaming Radius and the tip's Max Pick Tolerance of it, straight across at the camera's height, as OpenPnP's. Set tight (0.02 mm, 0.5 degrees) every part is measured again centred, at the cost of a look each. Each look is in the log ("look 2 of at most 3: off X, Y mm, turned A deg (seen W x H mm)"). A look tells the part's angle only within 45 degrees either way (with Rotation Full, 180), so looks that turn it further than that in all disagree with each other, and the alignment fails, saying so, rather than place it turned: a square part on a tip as wide as it, or wider, is seen round with the tip behind it, its angle anything. Use a smaller tip for such a part.

Fiducal Locator holds OpenPnP's ReferenceFiducialLocator settings: its default Vision Settings, Average Matches? (the passes after the first averaged, with three or more) and Max. Distance (old pipelines only) (mm, for a pipeline without a maxDistance stage). jplacer's own Measure Board Z? (off to begin with; OpenPnP keeps the Z a board was given) has a fiducial check set each board's or panel's Z as well, as OpenPnP's Estimate Object Z measures a height: the head camera looks at each fiducial found from 8 mm either side of it, along X and then along Y, and how far it seems to move against how far the camera moved gives the camera's scale there, and so, by its calibration at two heights, how far away it is; the board's Z is the mean of its fiducials' (the log says each, and warns when they differ by more than 0.3 mm: the board not flat or level, or a fiducial found where it is not). A camera calibrated at one height cannot tell heights, and the check then fails, saying so.

Fiducials are found by the vision settings' OpenPnP pipeline (see Vision), as OpenPnP finds them: the "results" stage's key point nearest where the fiducial should be, shown on the camera's view as it is found. Parts in bottom vision are found the same way, by the vision settings' OpenPnP pipeline: its rectangle for a part, shown on the camera's view as it is found.

Each also has a second tab, Bottom Vision Settings or Fiducial Vision Settings: the machine's default vision settings' own page, as the Vision tab shows it (its pipeline, sliders and tests), edited there too. Those settings belong to the job's configuration, not the machine: they are saved with it, and Undo on Machine Setup does not take them back.

docs.title: Signalers
docs.text:
A signaler is told how a job runs, as OpenPnP tells it: STOPPED when a job is started or stopped, RUNNING before each step, ERROR when a step fails, FINISHED when the job is done. New with Signalers chosen asks which kind:

Kind Settings SoundSignaler Play sound on error? and Play sound on completion?: a short falling sound when a job meets an error, a rising one when it is finished. ActuatorSignaler Actuator, switched on while the job is in its Job State and off otherwise (a beacon, a buzzer). With no job state chosen it is not switched. It is switched only when that changes what it was last switched to. Neoden4Signaler Play sound on error? and Play sound on completion?, each with a Test button: the buzzer of the machine's first NeoDen 4 controller (below) beeps, twice for 250 ms on an error, three times for 30 ms on a finish, again and again with the pause between, 10 seconds at first, 1.2 times shorter each time, until the Job error! or Job success! message is confirmed.

The sounds are played with the desktop's sound player (pw-play, paplay or aplay, the first installed); with none, the Log says so. As in OpenPnP, a file sounds/error.wav or sounds/success.wav in jplacer's settings folder (~/.config/jplacer) is played in place of jplacer's own.

docs.title: A NeoDen 4
docs.text:
A NeoDen 4 is driven as OpenPnP's NeoDen4Driver drives it: a controller whose Communications Type is neoden4 speaks the machine's own protocol on its serial port, and its firmware profile is neoden4 (chosen with it). Its NeoDen 4 group has Home Coordinate X and Home Coordinate Y (its X and Y axes' home coordinates, -437 and 437 on OpenPnP's) and Scale Factor - X and Scale Factor - Y (1.0501 and 1.04947526 to begin with): the machine moves X and Y in hundredths of a millimetre, times these.

  • Homing puts every nozzle up and lets the rotations go, then homes, once: homed again while connected, it only forgets the offsets, as OpenPnP's does. Nothing moves before it is homed.
  • Axes are known by their letters: X and Y; Z, U, V and W the Z of nozzles 1 to 4; A, B, C and D their rotations. A move turns the rotations that change, then moves the Zs that change, then X and Y, at the move's speed as a share of 250 mm/s, each followed by 100 ms; a move that fails is tried twice more, a second either side of clearing what the machine sent. Setting where X and Y are (after homing, or by a correction) offsets them.
  • Actuators are worked by their names, as OpenPnP's are: N1-Vacuum to N4-Vacuum (on, full vacuum; off, a puff of air for 100 ms, then none; read, the nozzle's air), N1-Blow to N4-Blow (set to a level, 127 blowing hardest; read as the vacuum), Lights-Down and Lights-Up (the cameras' lights; on, 3 and 1), Rails (a speed, negative backwards; on, 25) and ReleaseC (every rotation let go). Their commands are filled in when an OpenPnP machine is brought in.
  • A NeoDen 4 feeder actuator (OpenPnP's NeoDen4FeederActuator) has, under Properties, Peeler ID, Feeder ID, Feed Strength, Peel Strength and Peel length [%]: set to a length (a NeoDen 4 feeder actuates it with its pitch), it feeds that far, and the peeler peels Peel length % of five times it; 0 or less is refused. Change Feeder ID, with a New ID of 0 to 99 and Change, gives the feeder its Feeder ID names the new one (kept in the feeder), and the actuator then uses it.

Its cameras are read through the NeoDen's own camera library, libneodencam.so (on Windows NeoDen's NeodenCamera.dll), which must be installed where the system finds libraries (without it, the camera's window says it could not be loaded). Loaded the first time a NeoDen camera opens, its cameras are counted and the down and up ones (1 and 5) set to 1024 x 1024; the pictures are grey.

  • A Neoden4Camera (chosen on New with Cameras): its Device Settings have Camera Id (1 looks down, 5 up), Timeout (how long a picture may take, 1000 ms to begin with) and, under Image, Width and Height (1024) and Shift X and Shift Y (where on the sensor the picture starts, 0). A picture that does not come resets the camera.
  • A Neoden4SwitcherCamera: Source Camera (a Neoden4Camera, whose size and timeout it takes), Switcher Number (the NeoDen camera it reads), Exposure (25) and Gain (8). Each picture is taken from its camera at its exposure and gain; a change of either resets the camera first. Each has its own calibration, transforms and white balance, as OpenPnP's switcher cameras do.

An OpenPnP machine with a NeoDen4Driver comes in this way: its serial port, scale factors and command timeout, its connect wait (3 seconds unless set), its NeoDen 4 feeder actuators, its Neoden4Signaler, and its Neoden4Camera and Neoden4SwitcherCameras.

docs.title: Adding, removing and ordering parts
docs.text:
Over the tree are OpenPnP's tools for what is chosen: its own, then its group's. A driver, axis or actuator has Delete (the red cross), Permutate Up and Permutate Down (the arrows); a camera, signaler or head Delete; a nozzle Delete (the nozzle with a cross); a nozzle tip Unload, Load (on the nozzle chosen on the Jog panel, by the tip's changer steps) and Delete. Then the group's New (the green plus; a nozzle or nozzle tip with one in it). Each says what it does when pointed at; the tree's right-click menu has New and Delete too.

New adds a part of the kind chosen: with an axis (or Axes) chosen an axis, with a head's Nozzles chosen a nozzle, which goes on that head. A new part has a name saying what it is, to change, and an id of its own that stays the same whatever it is renamed to. Where there are several kinds (Axes, Drivers, a head's Nozzles, Cameras, Actuators, Signalers), New first asks which, as OpenPnP's Select Signaler... does (its button shows "…"). A controller is OpenPnP's NullDriver (jplacer's simulated controller, moving whatever axes are put on it), GcodeDriver or GcodeAsyncDriver (the same here: a G-code controller on a serial port, its commands queued either way) or NeoDen4Driver (a NeoDen 4); each new one is named after its kind. An axis is OpenPnP's ReferenceControllerAxis, ReferenceVirtualAxis, ReferenceMappedAxis, ReferenceCamCounterClockwiseAxis, ReferenceCamClockwiseAxis or ReferenceLinearTransformAxis (its Kind can be changed after). A nozzle is OpenPnP's ReferenceNozzle or ContactProbeNozzle (only that one has the Contact Probe tab); its Kind can be changed after, keeping its settings.

Delete asks first, as OpenPnP's ("Are you sure you want to delete ...?"), then removes the chosen part, unless something else uses it: an axis a nozzle or camera moves on, a controller an axis is on, an actuator that is a camera's light or a signaler's, a head with parts on it, a nozzle tip on a nozzle. Then nothing is removed, and the line at the bottom says what uses it. A nozzle tip that only fits nozzles is taken off their lists with it. Edit > Undo puts it back.

Permutate Up and Permutate Down move the chosen part among the others in its group. The order is the order they are shown in elsewhere (the cameras' tabs, the Axes panel).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
A part's settings are laid out as OpenPnP lays out the same part: in tabs, and in each tab in titled groups. Each setting has a control the size of what it holds: a box to tick, a number, a choice, a line of text. Choices of another part (the controller an axis is on, a nozzle's axes, a camera's light) are made by name. Coordinates are in columns under X, Y, Z and Rotation. A tab longer than its pane scrolls down; one wider (a nozzle tip's changer steps, say) scrolls across too, by the bar along its bottom (or the wheel with Shift held), its notes kept to the pane's width.

Part Tabs and groups Machine Configuration: General, in OpenPnP's order (name; Home after enabled?, the machine homing as soon as a connect you asked for succeeds (a cell that kept it on a controller keeps it here); Park after homed?, parking the head once homing, visual homing included, is done; Park all at Safe Z?, the Jog pad's Z park taking every Z on the head to safe Z before the tool's own (on to begin with); Auto tool select?, a camera, nozzle or actuator another panel or a running job moves (a camera taken to a feeder, a nozzle picking) chosen on the Jog panel, so the footprint drawn on a camera turns with it; Unsafe Z Roaming (10 mm to begin with, as OpenPnP's: a tool on a virtual Z axis, a camera's, left below safe Z and jogged further than this from where it was left low goes up to safe Z with that jog, so a later move does not bring it down unseen; a nozzle on a real Z axis is jogged where it is, however far, as OpenPnP does); Pool scripting engines?, as OpenPnP's: Python and JavaScript scripts run by interpreters kept from one to the next (see the Scripts menu); Auto-load most recent job?, the job open last opened again when jplacer starts: on for a new cell, as OpenPnP has it for an OpenPnP machine, off unless ticked there), Locations (Discard Location, where a nozzle drops a part that is not wanted; Default Board Location, where a board or panel added to a job starts). Motion Planner, as OpenPnP's: Allow uncoordinated? (off to begin with, as OpenPnP's: with continuous motion, a move by way of safe Z, up, across and down, planned as one sequence, the moves within the Safe Zone uncoordinated (free to stray from the straight line, each axis within its own limits and the zone) and the sequence optimized as OpenPnP's motion planner does: straight moves joined, a move up or down overshooting into the move across, so the head moves on while the nozzle is still rising or already falling; for a controller with Simulated3rdOrderControl or Full3rdOrderControl, as the others cannot follow such motion; an actuation, or anything that waits for the machine, sends what is planned first), Interpolation Retiming? (on to begin with, as OpenPnP's: an interpolated move, Simulated3rdOrderControl, stretched to take its planned time, its peak feed rate a little lower; off, the planned peak and a slightly shorter move), Minimum Speed [%] (5 to begin with: the Jog panel's speed goes no lower; also the least rate a controller is told, as OpenPnP's), and Allow continous motion? (off to begin with): a move no longer waits for the machine to stand still; the moves of one operation (up to safe Z, across, down) go to the controller back to back, and the machine is waited for only where it must stand still: an actuator that coordinates with it, a pick or place, homing, and the end of each operation. Test Motion: the First, Second, Third and Last Location, each with Enabled? and the place buttons, and between each two a Speed (a share of the machine's) and Safe Z? (by way of safe Z, or straight). Motion Planner Diagnostics: Test runs the tool chosen on the Jog panel to the first location, and once it stands there through the others, back from the last when it is nearer that one; then up to safe Z. Planned [s] is how long the run's moves take as planned from the axes' feed rates and accelerations, Actual how long they took; with Diagnostics? ticked, graphs of each axis's Location and Velocity over the run, from the controllers' reports. Simulation Mode, as OpenPnP's SimulationModeMachine: the machine's imperfections simulated, to try what overcomes them with no hardware. Simulation Mode Off, IdealMachine (none), StaticImperfectionsMachine (the homing error and non-squareness) or DynamicImperfectionsMachine (all). Replace Drivers? (on to begin with): while not Off, every controller is a simulated one (its axes' letters kept; the cell file keeps the real connection), from the next connect: one brought from OpenPnP is OpenPnP's GcodeServer, as OpenPnP simulates it (it takes the commands OpenPnP's controllers are set up with: it answers ok, moves its axes with G0 / G1 at once, homes them with G28 or $H to their home coordinates, sets where they are with G92, reports where they are to M114, says it is a GcodeServer to M115, and dwells for G4); jplacer's own controllers a simulated grblHAL. Nozzle Tip Runout and Runout Phase: an up-looking simulated camera sees each nozzle tip (its Diameter Seen From Below, else 1 mm) where its axes put it (the homing error is what a camera looking down sees, as in OpenPnP), going round on that radius as the nozzle turns; Non-Squareness Factor: a head camera sees X off by the factor times Y; Camera Lag [s]: what the cameras show is from that long ago; Camera Noise: up to that many faint sparks in each picture, so no two are alike (Camera Settling); Vibration Amplitude and Vibration Duration [s]: a head camera shakes along each move as it stops, that much at first, at 13.3 Hz, dying away to about 1% over the duration; Homing Error X and Y: a head camera sees the machine that far off until visual homing corrects it. A simulated camera with a light is dark while the light is off. Pick & Place Checking? (off to begin with), as OpenPnP's: with an image camera on the head (OpenPnP's test picture, say), each pick and place of a part is checked where the simulated machine has the nozzle (the homing error, non-squareness and runout in): the part's footprint, turned as the nozzle is, must match a part's body in the picture for a pick, its pads for a place, within the camera's tolerances (OpenPnP's: 0.1 mm, scoring at least 0.87 to pick and 0.58 to place), or the pick or place fails ("Nozzle N1 part R0805-1K pick location not recognized."); not near the discard location, and not for OpenPnP's TEST-OBJECT part. On a simulated controller, an actuator with no command for what is asked of it is switched with nothing sent, as on OpenPnP's NullDriver. An image camera not calibrated is taken as calibrated by its picture's scale (and its simulated turn, scale and mirroring). Machine Table Z and Set Machine Table Z give every feeder (a strip feeder's holes too), the job's boards and the cameras that Z; Reset Feeders sets every strip and blinds feeder's feed count back to 0. An OpenPnP SimulationModeMachine brings its settings in. Controller Configuration: Properties (name, firmware profile, or auto to recognise it; ); Sync Initial Location, as OpenPnP's: where the controller says it is is taken once connected, so the machine can be jogged before it is homed; and, with it, Allow Unhomed Motion (greyed until then): any move before homing, for a machine with absolute encoders; unhomed, without them a jog or move is refused saying which controller lacks which), Communications (Communications Type: serial or tcp, as OpenPnP's, neoden4 for a NeoDen 4 (see A NeoDen 4 above), or for a simulated controller (OpenPnP's NullDriver) simulated, changed to serial or tcp to drive the real one, as Issues & Solutions' Replace with GcodeDriver does (its axes, actuators and settings kept; Undo makes it simulated again); line endings: LF, CR or CRLF), Serial Port (Port: the serial ports there now, each by what the device says it is, kept by its stable /dev/serial/by-id name; the one set, while it is not plugged in, listed as "(not found)"; baud, parity, data bits, stop bits, flow control, and Set DTR / Set RTS to raise those lines once the port is open) or, over TCP, TCP (IP Address, an address or host name, and Port, 23 to begin with, as a controller on Ethernet such as grblHAL's listens; a connection not made in 5 seconds is given up). Driver Settings: Motion Control Type, as OpenPnP's: how a move is planned (OpenPnP's motion planner: each axis's motion profile, of constant jerk segments, solved for the shortest time its feed rate, acceleration and jerk allow, the axes in a straight line together) and what this controller is told of it. ToolpathFeedRate: the Max. Feed Rate times the speed, no acceleration (the controller's own); EuclideanAxisLimits: the axes' feed rate, acceleration and jerk limits times the speed (over the move as G-code reads F, so a diagonal can go faster), the ramps left to the controller; ConstantAcceleration: planned for a controller with constant acceleration, told the feed rate and acceleration the move reaches; ModeratedConstantAcceleration: the move planned with jerk control, sent as one constant acceleration move taking the same time; SimpleSCurve: planned for simplified S-curves (no constant acceleration phase: TinyG, Marlin); Simulated3rdOrderControl: jerk control simulated on a constant acceleration controller by interpolating the move into short steps (a GcodeAsyncDriver: its Advanced Settings' Interpolation: at most Maximum Number of Steps a move, 32 to begin with, else one moderated move and the log says so; the acceleration ramped in Maximum Number of Jerk Steps, 4; Minimum Step Time [s], 0.001; Minimum Axis Resolution Ticks, 16; Maximum Junction Deviation, 0.02 mm); Full3rdOrderControl: for a controller with full jerk control. A new controller starts with ToolpathFeedRate, as OpenPnP's; a cell kept before this was a setting keeps how its moves were sent, EuclideanAxisLimits; an OpenPnP import brings its own. The feed rate, acceleration and jerk go into the move command's {feed}, {acceleration} and {jerk}, left out with their letter where the type does not set them. Max. Feed Rate (the fastest any move is sent; 0 for no cap), Log G-code? (as OpenPnP's: the G-code sent also written to a file of its own, GcodeDriver/<name>-<time>.g beside the settings; the log and the Console have the traffic anyway), Letter Variables? (on, to begin with: a move names each axis by its letter, {axes}; off, as OpenPnP's: by its type, {X} {Y} {Z} {Rotation} in the controller's move command, one axis of each type a command, several of a type, two nozzles' Zs, moved one after another, a type not in a move left out with its letter), Allow Pre-Move Commands? (with Letter Variables off only, as OpenPnP refuses both: each moving axis's Pre-Move Command, set on the axis, sent first with {Coordinate} where it was, to switch an output several axes share to it; axes sharing a letter keep where they were last sent, as the controller's report cannot tell them apart), Units (Millimeters or Inches, as OpenPnP's: the controller's coordinates, feed rate, acceleration and jerk sent in them and its reports read back from them, rotations staying degrees; its start-up command must tell it so, G20 or G21), OpenPnP's Backslash Escaped Characters? (\t, \b, \n, \r, \f and \uXXXX in a command sent as the characters they stand for), Remove Comments? ((...) and from ; on left out), Compress G-code? (spaces and a number's trailing zeros left out: G1 X100.0000 Y20.1000 goes as G1X100Y20.1) Send FeedRate On Change Only?, Send Acceleration On Change Only? and Send Jerk On Change Only? (a move's {feed}, {acceleration} or {jerk}, with the letter before it, left out when it is within a thousandth of the one last sent, as the controller keeps it; sent again after connecting and homing) and Compression Exclude Characters ([]" to begin with: from the first to the last of them is sent as written), the timeouts and the status interval; $-Command Wait Time [ms], as OpenPnP's (after a command beginning with $, a grbl setting written to its memory, is confirmed, the next waits this long; 50 to begin with); Detect Firmware, as OpenPnP's, asks the connected controller again what it runs (its profile chosen again with auto), and Firmware shows what it said (it does not connect by itself); State is what the controller says it is doing now (Idle, Run, Hold, Alarm…) or not connected, kept up to date; Keep Alive, as OpenPnP's: Disconnect leaves this controller's connection open (a board that resets as its port is opened is not reset again), and the next Connect takes it up as it is, without identifying it again (losing the connection, an error, or closing the cell still closes it; Issues & Solutions warns to use it only when necessary). Gcode: the firmware's commands by what they are for (Connecting: Start-up, Unlock; Homing: Home, Set Position; Moving: Move, Rapid Move, Wait for Moves, Dwell; Outputs: Output On, Output Off; anything else under Other), each group saying what its {placeholders} are; empty, the profile's is used, shown greyed (with auto, each profile's, those that agree named together), else what is written here, several lines if need be; and OpenPnP's Import / Export: Export Gcode File writes the controller, as set up here, to a file (a .json, asking before replacing one), and Copy Gcode to Clipboard copies the same text. Console, as OpenPnP's: the Gcode console, what was last sent to this controller (→) and what it answered (←), newest at the bottom, as it happens; a Command line: sent to it with Return or Send (Up and Down bring back the lines sent before), made upper case first with Force Upper Case (ticked to begin with) Axis Configuration: Properties (kind: driven by a controller, mapped to follow another axis through two points, a cam (OpenPnP's cam axes: a Z that a cam on a rotation axis drives, Z = Cam Radius x sin(angle + 90 - Cam Arms Angle / 2), plus an old cam wheel's radius and gap; Clockwise? for the cam's other nozzle, which goes down as the first comes up; kept to the cam's useful range), linear (OpenPnP's linear transform axis: its coordinate is each input axis's, X, Y, Z and Rotation, times its Factor, plus the Offset; the linear axes of a move, with the tool's other ones held where they are, are solved back onto their inputs together, as OpenPnP inverts its transform, so a turned or skewed head moves straight in its own coordinates), or virtual; type; name), Controller Settings (driver, axis letter, home coordinate; Switch Linear ↔ Rotational?, for a controller axis used the other way round from its type (a linear one driving a rotation, or the reverse): a move's feed rate is sent as G-code reads F, over the linear axes' path, or the rotational ones' when nothing linear moves, the move as long as its slowest axis takes, and the controller's Max Feed Rate only for linear moves; Resolution, what one motor step moves it, and its other side Steps / mm, every move going to the nearest whole step (at a soft limit, the step on this side of it); a rotation axis's Limit to Range, keeping it within -180..180, and Wrap Around, turning the short way round: with both, it turns the short way and its controller is then told the same angle within the range), Axis Mapping (input axis, map points A and B), Kinematic Settings (soft limits and safe zone, each with Enabled?; feed rate per second and per minute; acceleration and jerk, which reach a controller whose move command takes {acceleration} or {jerk}, scaled with the move's speed). Backlash Compensation: the method (None, OneSidedPositioning, DirectionalCompensation, DirectionalSneakUp), its offset, sneak-up distance and speed factor, Calibrate (an X or Y axis), and the last calibration's tolerance and graphs (see Backlash). Periodic Error (an X or Y controller axis): its drive's period, the correction in use, Scan Board, Apply, Clear, and the last scan (see Periodic error) Head Configuration: Properties (name), Locations (homing fiducial, its diameter and homing method; Homing Fiducial Part, the library part visual homing looks for the mark as, chosen from the library's parts ((none) to begin with, and when the one chosen has been deleted), kept by the part itself so renaming it changes nothing; the list follows the library as it changes; with Visual Test (the homing fiducial looked for without changing the machine's coordinates) and Visual Home, and OpenPnP's notice: mount and set up the homing fiducial early, as every place captured since is broken when it changes or moves; park location), Calibration Rig, as OpenPnP's (X, Y, Z and Diameter of the Primary Fiducial, at the PCB surface's Z, and the Secondary Fiducial, at a different Z: a head camera is calibrated again over the secondary fiducial to measure it at a second height; the Test Object Diameter and Test Object Thickness of the test object the nozzles' precise offsets are calibrated with, lying on the primary fiducial (0 thick: paper-thin), and Calibrate Nozzles at Two Heights?, the nozzle carrying it to the secondary fiducial as well, for the nozzle's lean; a test object kept before as its top's Z is read as its thickness above the primary fiducial; a head's places have X, Y and Z and no rotation, so capturing with or moving the nozzle leaves the Diameter alone), Z Probe (Z Probe Actuator, as OpenPnP's: wherever Capture Camera Location captures a place, on a feeder's page or here, the probe goes over it by way of safe Z, is read, in millimetres from where it is, and goes back, and the reading fills in the place's Z), Pump (the vacuum pump's actuator; Pump Control, as OpenPnP's: None, controlled by hand or outside jplacer; PartOn, on when a part is about to be picked, off when no nozzle holds one; TaskDuration, off only once the queued work (the running job) is done and no nozzle holds a part; KeepRunning, on until switched off or the machine is disabled; Pump On Wait [ms], how long it takes to come up: as OpenPnP's, waited each time the pump is switched on, before the nozzle's valve opens, and said in the log and Console so a long one, a reservoir brought up to pressure, does not look like a stall) Nozzle Configuration: Properties (name; Kind, ReferenceNozzle or ContactProbeNozzle, the one that finds heights by touch on its Contact Probe tab: with Method VacuumSense, it steps down a Sniffle Increment at a time until its tip's part-off check finds the nozzle blocked, which needs a vacuum and a vacuum sensing actuator on the nozzle and a Part-Off method on the tip), Coordinate System (head; axes and offsets; the Lean (per mm of Z), X and Y and the Z it holds from, as calibrated at two heights and to be set by hand (0 and 0: none; a move with no Z works its X and Y out for the Z the nozzle is at); OpenPnP's Safe Z, shown not set: where its Z is at the Z axis's Safe Zone Low, or a virtual Z's home coordinate), Offsets Calibrated (when its X and Y offsets were last calibrated here, how long ago, and how: roughly on the primary fiducial, or precisely with the test object; "never, in jplacer" until then), Settings (pick and place dwell times), Safe Z (Dynamic Safe Z, as OpenPnP's: carrying a part, the nozzle's safe Z is raised by the part's height, so the part's bottom is at the safe zone's low end, as far as the zone allows; for a nozzle on a Z axis of its own), Rotation (Rotation Mode, as OpenPnP's: while the nozzle holds a part its rotation reads the part's angle, its rotation axis turned that much less by the rotation mode offset (the Jog panel and the status bar show the part's angle; none again once the part is placed or dropped). AbsolutePartAngle, no offset: the axis at the part's own angle at pick and at place; PlacementAngle, the offset the placement's angle, so the axis is at 0 at place; MinimalRotation, picked at whatever angle the axis has; LimitedArticulation, for a nozzle that turns only so far (its rotation axis limited to range, within its soft limits), the offset so the turn from pick to place, with Max. Pick Articulation and Max. Alignment Articulation to spare, sits about the middle of the range. Align with Part?, OpenPnP's aligning rotation mode: bottom vision's turn of the part taken into the offset, so the nozzle reads the part's angle as aligned). Nozzle Tips: every tip, whether it is Compatible? and whether it is Loaded?. Vacuum: the vacuum actuator, the blow-off actuator and whether it closes the vacuum itself, the sensing actuator. Tool Changer, as OpenPnP's: Automatic Tool Changer Enabled? (on, a tip change runs the tips' load and unload steps; off, or for a tip without steps, the nozzle goes up to safe Z, and to its Manual Change Location when one is set, and you are asked to change the tip by hand, in OpenPnP's words, the job going on once you say it is done; off for a nozzle brought in from OpenPnP unless it was on there), Change On Manual Pick? (a pick on the Feeders tab with a tip that does not fit the part's package puts on one that does and no nozzle has, and measures the tip put on as its Auto Recalibration says before it picks, as every tip change by the changer does; without it, or with none to put on, the pick is refused, saying which nozzle has a fitting tip). Homing: the Home Command that homes this nozzle's Z alone, and Home Z to run it (see Homing a nozzle's Z). Calibration: measures where the nozzle is on the head (its X and Y offsets), and keeps its last 10 calibrations. Precise Offsets, by the Test Object is the precise calibration Issues & Solutions also offers (see Issues & Solutions): the nozzle picks a small round test object off the head's primary calibration fiducial at each of the machine's nozzle offset angles round the circle, placing it turned 180 degrees each time, and the camera finds it after each; each angle gives its own estimate of how far the offsets are off, and their mean is the correction made. With Two Heights?, the nozzle then carries the object to the secondary fiducial, does the same there, and carries it back: the two corrections give the nozzle's lean, how far its tip moves in X and Y for each mm its Z goes up or down (a Z axis not quite square to the table). The offsets are kept at the height they were calibrated at, and every move of the nozzle (picks, places, jogs, the tip changer, bottom vision, captures and the position shown) takes its X and Y offsets at the Z it goes to, the lean added; one height keeps the lean found before. The camera must be calibrated at two heights to see the object on the secondary fiducial. Test Object Diameter with Detect (as Issues & Solutions' Auto-Detect Next: the round feature where the camera looks now, its size by the camera's scale; again, the next one it sees; Calibrate uses the size as set and does not measure it again), Test Object Thickness with Capture (its top above the fiducial it lies on, where the nozzle picks and places it: the nozzle's Z with its tip touching the object on the primary fiducial, less the fiducial's Z; 0, paper-thin), Two Heights? (greyed without a secondary fiducial), and Calibrate (greyed until the head has its primary fiducial and the test object's diameter). Last Calibration: when and how, the offsets before and the ones found (at the height calibrated at), the change, the Lean (in mm of X and Y per mm of Z; over 0.02 a note says to look for a bent tip or a loose Z carriage), and at each height how closely the angles agree and the outliers: an angle further from their mean than 3 times the angles' median distance from it (and at least 0.01 mm). For each height a graph draws each angle's estimate about their mean, outliers in their own colour outside the outlier limit circle, with a table of each angle's X, Y and distance; a tight cluster is a good run, one point on its own a bad find or the object slipping on the tip, all of them round a ring the tip's runout. Calibrations, Run by Run: every kept calibration, newest first (how, the offsets found, the change, the outliers), and a graph of each earlier precise run's offsets against the last one's, to see how well runs repeat. A rough calibration on the primary fiducial (Issues & Solutions) and one by a mark are kept as runs too. Placement Check (Check Placement) checks the whole chain as a job places, changing nothing: the nozzle picks the test object off the primary fiducial and puts it back unturned three times (how far it moves each time is the pick and the let-go alone: the drift), then at 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees, twice round, aligns it on the camera looking up as a job aligns a part (turned to the angle first, the nozzle over the camera less its tip's camera offset, the object found round), puts it back on the fiducial with the job's own correction, and the head camera finds where it landed. Shown: where it landed on average (Lands Off By), and its pieces, each measured on its own: the Drift, Bottom Vision's Bias (its offsets' mean: where the object truly sits on the nozzle turns with the angle and averages away), and the Offset Error at Place Height (the average less the drift, plus vision's bias); what Turns With the Angle (runout, the rotation's centre), the Test Object's Own Offset (the centre the head camera finds on its top against the one bottom vision finds underneath, as a dot printed off the object's middle gives: it turns as the object is turned, picked unturned and put down turned each time, so a fit over the placements tells it apart and takes it out of the rest; over about 0.05 mm, a matching object gives a cleaner check) and what is Left Over; every find's picture is kept, with where the object was looked for and where it was found drawn on it, in a folder for the check beside the vision debug pictures (log/vision, beside the settings), and each find's numbers are in the log; a graph of each landing and the drifts, and a table of each placement (where bottom vision saw it on the nozzle, where it landed, what is left over). The last check is kept with the nozzle, saved to the machine's file as soon as it is made (as are the other measurements: a camera's settling trace and tuned values, a tip's last vacuum readings, a controller's detected firmware). Rough Offsets, by a Mark: lower the nozzle into putty (or the like) where it leaves a mark, Store Nozzle Mark Position, move the camera over the centre of the mark, Calculate Nozzle Offset; the offsets change by how far the camera is from where the nozzle thought it was. Each calibration is one step to undo. As OpenPnP's, whenever a nozzle's X and Y offsets change (here, or typed), what depends on them follows in the same step: every nozzle tip's runout is forgotten (it was measured against the old offsets; a change of no more than 0.01 mm keeps it), the nozzle's manual tip change location moves by the same, an actuator or camera on the head with the nozzle's old X and Y offsets (fastened to it, as a push-pull feeder's actuator) takes the new ones, and for the head's first nozzle the cameras looking up move by the same (they were most likely calibrated with it); offsets that were not set (all zero) move nothing else. Tip changer steps are in the axes' own coordinates and stay as they are. Contact Probe (a ContactProbeNozzle only), OpenPnP's ContactProbeNozzle: Method None, ContactSenseActuator (the Contact Sense Actuator switched on is the controller's probing move down until contact, G38.2 or the like, and off its retract; the nozzle's Z is then where the controller says it stopped) or VacuumSense (the nozzle stepped down a Sniffle Increment at a time, waiting Sniffle Dwell Time [ms], until its tip's part-off check finds the nozzle blocked); Probe Speed (for the probing command), Start Offset above where the surface should be, Probe Depth below it, Final Adjustment (up for overshoot, down for spring tension); Feeder Height Probing and Placement Height Probing, Off, Once, AfterHoming or EachTime; Discard Probing, a discard (a job's, or the Jog panel's) probing down into the discard place from the tip's tallest part above it (there must be something soft or slanted there, to brush the part off), retracting, and letting go there. With the contact sense actuator, a job probes each feeder's pick height and each part's place height so (a part of unknown height probed from the tallest its tip takes, and its height kept), and uses the offset it found for the next ones; heights kept while jplacer runs, those probed AfterHoming forgotten on homing; the Nozzle.BeforePickProbe, AfterPickProbe, BeforePlaceProbe and AfterPlaceProbe scripting events round each probe.
