Nozzle tip Configuration: Properties (name), Pick & Place (its pick and place dwell times, added to the nozzle's; Approach Height, Approach Speed (%) and Lift Speed (%): every pick and place with the tip (a job's, the Jog panel's, a calibration's, Check Placement's) goes down at the Z axis's speed to that height above, the last of the way at the approach's share of it, and after the vacuum the same distance up at the lift's share, then up to safe Z; a nozzle sent down to a working height below safe Z by hand (the Jog panel's Position Nozzle, a Position button) comes the last of the way down at the approach's share too; a tip meeting the part a touch early meets it slowly instead of driving into its spring and skidding the part, and the lift does not snatch a part the vacuum still holds a moment; 0 high, straight down and up; Place Blow-Off Level, as OpenPnP's: at place, the nozzle's blow-off actuator is switched on, or set to the level when it takes a value, at the part's package's Blow Off Level, else this one; 0 for both, no blow-off, only the vacuum off. At pick, a package's Vacuum Level is what a vacuum actuator taking a value is set to), Push and Drag Usage (Push & Drag allowed?, for a tip sturdy enough to push a blinds feeder's cover; its Outside Diameter at its lowest 0.75 mm), Part Dimensions (diameter seen from below; Min. Part Diameter, the smallest part it picks, at least its air bore plus twice the pick tolerance; Max. Part Height, taken as the height of a part whose height is not known when Dynamic Safe Z lifts it; Max. Part Diameter, the largest part it picks, its diagonal with tolerances, which bounds what bottom vision masks round it; Max. Pick Tolerance, how far off a part may be picked, which is how far bottom vision looks, unless the part's package sets its own), Nozzles (the nozzles it fits). Part Detection, as OpenPnP's: Part On Vacuum Sensing and Part Off Vacuum Sensing, each with a Measurement Method (None; Absolute, the vacuum read within the Vacuum Range's Low..High Value; Difference: for part on, the level at the end of the pick's dwell within the Vacuum Range and the change since within the Difference Range; for part off, the level just before the check within the Vacuum Range and the change through it within the Difference Range; Ratio, for a vacuum sensor on the pump's side of the valve, which reads the pump while the valve is closed: the level as a share of the pump's, read just before (part on: before the pick's valve opened; part off: before the pulse), within the Vacuum Range, given to the thousandth, so the pump's own swings, a reservoir switched between two pressures, say, do not count), Establish Level? (the pick's dwell ends as soon as the vacuum has built up into the Vacuum Range, the place's as soon as it has decayed into it), and Perform Checks?: part on After Pick (a pick that fails it is tried again, as the feeder's pick retries say), after Alignment and Before Place; part off After Place and Before Pick, at safe Z; a failing check stops the placement, with OpenPnP's words ("No part vacuum-detected after pick.", "Part vacuum-detected on nozzle before pick.", and so on). Part off is checked by a pulse: the valve open for Valve open/close (ms)'s first time, the vacuum read through it, then closed for its second. The Last Reading of each (and its difference) is shown, and with a difference or Establish Level a graph of the vacuum and the valve over the last pick (place) and check. Checks need the nozzle's vacuum sense actuator (Issues & Solutions says so). The ranges are measured rather than guessed: each has a Measure row, shown whatever the method. Part Off's Measure (its Valve open/close (ms) beside it, which it needs: with no open time there is no pulse, and it says so) takes the nozzle up to safe Z with nothing on it (a part jplacer takes to be on it discarded first) and makes the part-off check's pulse 20 times, half a second apart, reading the level before each, as the valve closes, and after the Valve close wait. Part On's Without Part (up at safe Z, nothing on the nozzle) and With Part (a part picked, or held to the tip, where it is) switch the vacuum on as a pick does, wait the pick's dwell, read the level 20 times over 3 seconds, and switch it off again (a part held is let go there, and jplacer no longer takes it to be on the nozzle). Each range is told apart from the other state's level: Part On's, a part held from none; Part Off's, an open nozzle from a blocked one, whose level is Part On's With Part (and, with Difference, the level before the pulse from the pump pulled down by an open nozzle, Part On's Without Part). Its edge towards the other is halfway between the two (a few seconds' deviations say whether the two can be told apart, not where the line goes: a pump switched on and off by a pressure switch moves a level far more over its cycle), and it reaches the other way as far again as the level itself, so the pump's level drifting (by thousands over minutes on some machines) does not leave it. Two levels fewer than 6 deviations apart cannot be told apart by that method: when the other method (Absolute or Difference) tells them apart it is set instead, and said; when neither does, no range is set, and it says so. Without the other state measured, the range is 6 deviations either side of the mean (at least the readings' spread and one step of the reading), and it says what to measure. A level that comes most of the way back as the valve closes means the sensor reads the pump's side of the valve, not the nozzle: Valve close is set to 0 (whether or not ranges are set), so the check reads the level as the valve closes. Each level is also taken as a share of the pump's just before (Part On reads the pump before its valve opens); where the shares come out under 1, the sensor reads the pump's side of the valve and Ratio is set, its range told apart the same way, when it tells the two apart. A method of None becomes Absolute (Ratio on the pump's side). Measuring Part On sets Part Off's ranges again too. The ranges are set as one step to undo, what was measured is kept with the tip and shown under the buttons (when, mean, deviation, lowest and highest), and a dialog gives the numbers and the ranges set, or why none were. A pick or place from a script, or the Jog panel's Special tab, checks nothing, as OpenPnP's; the Feeders tab's pick checks before and after, and a feeder's take back after. Tool Changer: the tip's changer steps as tables, as many as the change takes (OpenPnP's changer has four places, which cannot go round a row of holders; an OpenPnP import brings them as its first four moves, with its Post actuators between): Loading, each row a step, its Kind (move, safe Z, actuator, wait, ask); a move its X, Y, Z and Rotation (one left empty stays as it is: a move with no Z keeps the height, so at Safe Z it goes over the other holders), with the place buttons, its Speed [%] (a share of the machine's, the move to it), Safe Z? (up to Safe Z, across, then down to its Z; without, straight there) and Backlash? (compensated as every other move; without, none of the compensation that goes past the place and back); an actuator which and on or off; a wait how long; an ask its message. Each row's buttons, before its number: add a step after it (a move copies its place, speed and Backlash?), delete it, move it up, move it down, each a step to undo. Loading takes each step in turn, then goes up to Safe Z. Unloading as loading backwards lists the steps it works out, to check. Unloading: loading backwards, or steps of its own, a second table of the same kind (starting as loading backwards, to change from there): to unload from the park place by the middle of the machine first, say. Then OpenPnP's Vision Calibration, as OpenPnP's: the Vision Location (None, or the First, Second, Third or Last Location, or the Touch Location; with steps of jplacer's own, the first and last moves), Adjust Z (added to its Z, for the camera's scale there), Calibration Trigger (Manual, MachineHome, NozzleTipChange), Template Width and Template Height, Tolerance, Wanted Precision, Max. Passes, Minimum Score with the Last Score and Test, and Template Empty and Template Occupied, each with Capture (the head camera over the Vision Location, the middle of its picture, Template Width by Height, kept as a PNG file beside the cell file, in org.openpnp.vision.TemplateImage, and shown) and Reset. Before a tip is loaded or unloaded by its changer, its slot is found: the head camera over the Vision Location, both templates looked for in the middle of the picture, Tolerance larger than a template; under Minimum Score, or the slot found occupied when it should be empty (the tip on a nozzle) or empty when it should be occupied, the change stops; otherwise the camera is centred on it and it is looked for again, until a pass moves less than the Wanted Precision (at most Max. Passes; further off than the Tolerance stops it). How far off the slot was moves every place of that change. It is worked out the first time it is needed after jplacer starts, again on every change with NozzleTipChange, and again after homing unless Manual; Test finds it afresh and shows how far off it was and its score. Cloning Settings: Behavior Template (one tip only), Clones from Template or Locked; the template's Clone Tool Changer Settings to all Nozzle Tips, and a clone's Clone Tool Changer Settings from Template, give a tip, as Locations?, Z Calibration? and Vision Calibration? say (all ticked to begin with, for the session), the template's loading and unloading steps and its touch location, each place moved by how far the tip's own first move is from the template's, its Z calibration settings (when and Fail Homing?), and its Vision Calibration settings and templates (a locked tip, or one without a first move, is left as it is; Clone from Template is greyed for a locked tip, or with no template). The template's Calibrate all Touch Locations' Z to Template (greyed for any other tip): the template tip is loaded on the default probing nozzle (the first that probes by contact), its Z calibrated at its own touch location, then every other tip's touch location (one set, and not of a tip whose name begins unloaded; locked tips too) is probed with it, and its Z set to where it was met: one step to undo. Where a nozzle probes by contact, OpenPnP's Z Calibration: Touch At, the tip's own Touch Location or the Primary Fiducial (the head's, from its Calibration Rig: probed on the fiducial's surface, so nothing may lie on it then; every tip set so touches at the one place, which moves with the rig, and its X, Y and Z are shown in place of the Touch Location's; Calibrate all Touch Locations' Z to Template leaves such tips out, having no place of their own to set); the Touch Location (with Set? and the place buttons, and Contact Probe Tool, after asking, as it changes the Z reference: the default probing nozzle, its Z calibration forgotten, probes there and the Z it met is put in the place), Auto Z Calibration, when (Manual, MachineHome once homed, NozzleTipChange once homed and on each load), beside it the calibrated Z offset of the nozzle the tip is on (empty until calibrated), Reset and Calibrate now, and, when not Manual, Fail Homing? (a calibration failing once homed fails the homing): the nozzle the tip is on probes the touch location from its Start Offset, and how far from its Z it met it (with the Final Adjustment; at most the nozzle's 2 mm largest offset) moves every Z of that nozzle while the tip stays on it. A calibration that cannot be made says why in a dialog: with no nozzle carrying the tip, or, probing by VacuumSense, a tip with no Part Off Vacuum Sensing method (the probe steps down until the part-off check finds the nozzle blocked, so it needs one). Calibration: runout (below), and OpenPnP's Background Calibration: Method (None, Brightness, or BrightnessAndKeyColor for a tip in a vivid key colour on a dark background), Minimum Detail Size (the smallest detail of a part: bottom vision blurs and samples at half of it), and the Hue, Saturation and Value range found, each with a Tolerance it is widened by. Under them, OpenPnP's colour wheel of the ranges (hue round it, saturation out from the middle; the colours in the hue and saturation ranges bright, the rest dimmed to the least value; without colour when the Method is None) and beside it a bar of the values (bright at the top, those out of range faded). Calibrating the runout measures it too, from the pictures of the tip all round (its middle blotted out); what it says of them shows beside the wheel, a line between each finding, and Show Problems shows the pictures where the background would not be masked beside the same with that marked, on the camera looking up. Bottom vision masks the background so (MaskHsv) for parts on the tip. Camera General Configuration: Properties (name, looking down or up; Preview FPS, how many times a second the live picture is shown at most, 0 every picture; Suspend during tasks?, the live picture held still while the machine moves or a job runs, only what vision shows then; Warn if camera calibration is not completed (on to begin with): its live picture crossed out in red, with "Not calibrated for its W×H pictures" over it, while the camera has no calibration for that picture size (what is measured through it cannot be trusted); Auto Camera View?, the camera brought to the front when vision shows a result on it, a panel moves it to look somewhere, or a tool is moved by hand (Position Tool, Move Selected Nozzle to Camera, a jog) to within 50 mm of it, as OpenPnP's (a nozzle over the camera looking up brings that camera forward); Show in multi camera view?, as OpenPnP's: off, the camera's window starts closed (a capture card's camera already shown through SwitcherCameras, say), to be opened from View, or by anything that looks through it; as OpenPnP's, an OpenPnP camera's preview rate its fps), Light (light actuator: for a camera on a head, one of the head's, or with Allow Machine Actuators? (as OpenPnP's, for older scripts' lights) one of the machine's too; ON Before Capture?, before a picture for vision, and User Camera Action?, while you look at the camera, and, as OpenPnP's, when a move you make (a jog, Position Tool, Move Selected Nozzle to Camera, a click in a camera's picture) takes a tool to within 50 mm of it, on screen or not and whatever its Auto Camera View?, staying on until switched off by hand (its light toggle); OFF After Capture?, after the picture for vision, and Anti-Glare?, while another camera takes one), Units Per Pixel (a rough scale to start calibrating from). Camera Settling: how a picture for vision (calibrating, visual homing and testing, locating a board) waits for the camera to stop after a move: FixedTime, a set time after the move; or Maximum, Mean, Euclidean or Square, comparing each picture with the one before (as a percentage of full scale), or Motion (how many pixels the picture moved: its middle looked for in the one before), until the difference stays under the Settle Threshold for the Debounce Frames (a picture exactly like the one before does not count, as OpenPnP's), within the Settle Timeout (on a timeout the last picture is used, and the log warns, each time, with the least difference seen against the threshold; a least difference above the threshold means the picture's own noise is more than it allows, so the camera can never settle and every look waits out the timeout: raise Denoise (Pixel) until the flat line the Here test draws is under the threshold (a camera's grain, more so with a high Sharpness, is blurred away; a USB camera at 1280×720 may need about 21), else raise Settle Threshold just above that line. OpenPnP only notes a timeout in its debug log). As OpenPnP's, each picture is first made grey unless Color Sensitive?, cut to the Center Mask (a circle of that share of the picture's smaller side; 0 all of it), its contrast stretched by Enhance Contrast (0 none, 1 to the full range), blurred by Denoise (Pixel) (a Gaussian that many pixels across; a large one on the picture scaled down), and with Edge Sensitive? its edges taken (the gradients rather than the brightness). With Diagnostics?, every settle (vision's too) is graphed here, with when each picture was taken, and its pictures, as compared, can be stepped through with Replay. A Test: a camera on a head moved one jog step (the Jog pad's distance) Left, Right, Back or Front and back, or not at all (Here); for a fixed camera, the nozzle chosen on the Jog pad moved so instead (put it there, at the camera's focus, first: only X and Y move), or turned one jog step and back (Rotate), or (Up) brought over the camera at Safe Z (already within 5 mm of it, up to Safe Z and back), the settling being the head's as that camera sees it; then let settle, with a graph of each picture's difference from the one before against time, the threshold and when it was taken to be still (with FixedTime, the Euclidean difference over the fixed wait). Device Settings: for OpenPnP's MjpgCaptureCamera (chosen on New: a camera on the network sending a stream of JPEGs over HTTP), its MJPG URL (http://host:port/path) and Timeout; for OpenPnP's ImageCamera (chosen on New: a camera that shows the part of a picture of the table under where it looks, to try jobs and vision without a camera), as OpenPnP's: Camera Simulation, its Pixel Dimension (the view's size), Simulated Units per Pixel (the picture's own) and Offset (where the picture's bottom left is), Z Rotation (its mounting turn), Y Rotation (a sideways tilt), Viewing Scale, Distortion [%] (the lens's: barrel when positive, pincushion when negative), View mirrored? and Source URL (a PNG; Browse chooses one), and Simulated Calibration Rig: Focal Length and Sensor Diagonal (the lens and sensor, 6 and 4.4 mm to begin with) and a Primary Fiducial and Secondary Fiducial (X, Y, Z; none at the origin), each a 1 mm white dot drawn into the picture where it is, the secondary at its own height (as far from the camera as the lens and sensor make it, bigger or smaller, blurred, and moved by the tilt), to try the camera's calibration; for OpenPnP's GstreamerCamera (chosen on New: any GStreamer pipeline), its Pipeline launch string, as gst-launch-1.0 is given one (v4l2src device=/dev/video0 ! image/jpeg,width=1280,height=720 ! jpegdec): its pictures, turned to colour, are the camera's, at the size and rate the pipeline gives (GStreamer must be installed on the computer); for OpenPnP's OnvifIPCamera (chosen on New: an IP camera set up over ONVIF), its Camera IP (ip:port), Username and Password (sent as a WS-Security digest), Resolution (one of those the camera offers, listed once it has been opened; empty for its largest: its first JPEG profile is set to it, at its best quality and fastest rate), and Target Width and Target Height (each snapshot resized to them; 0 for none): its pictures are its snapshots, fetched one after another; for OpenPnP's Neoden4Camera and Neoden4SwitcherCamera, see A NeoDen 4 above; for OpenPnP's SimulatedUpCamera (one brought in from an OpenPnP machine), as OpenPnP's, its Camera Simulation: Camera Location (where it physically is, X, Y, Z and Rotation: where it is set up to be until changed here, so its calibration can be tried against a camera that is not quite where it is said to be), Pixel Dimension, Simulated Units per Pixel, Focal Length and Sensor Diagonal (a nozzle or part above or below its focus seen nearer its middle, smaller or bigger, and darker or brighter, as through that lens; beyond twice the lens's distance, not at all), Background Scenario (the shade behind and the nozzle tip's colour: Black, Dark, Green, Magenta, BlackAndDark, DarkAndGrey, DarkAndBlueTint, to try background calibration), Pick Error Offsets (X, Y and Rotation: a part shown that far off on its nozzle, to try bottom vision), View mirrored? (a camera looking up sees the machine mirrored; ticked, mirrored back) and Simulate Focal Blur? (what is out of focus blurred, as for trying Auto Focus); it shows the nozzles and the parts on them (their undersides a part's height below the tip, 1 mm when not known) whether or not the machine is in Simulation Mode; for OpenPnP's SwitcherCamera (chosen on New: one of several analog cameras on one capture device through a multiplexer), its Source Camera (the capture device's camera, whose pictures, as taken, are this camera's: it has its own calibration, transforms and white balance), Switcher Number (cameras on the same multiplexer share one), and the Actuator set to Actuator Value to switch it in (a boolean actuator: on for any value but 0), then Actuator Delay waited before its pictures are its own; it switches itself in when vision takes its picture, and when it starts showing, and otherwise waits, keeping its last picture; the source camera runs while the machine is on, as every camera does; for a capture device, device (the name it gives itself, found in whichever socket it is in, or its node, /dev/video2: an OpenPnP OpenCvCamera's index comes in so, its OpenCV capture properties as the camera's own Properties where they are one, and an OpenPnP Webcam by its name), its Format, as OpenPnP's: one of the formats the camera offers, each its picture size, frames per second and kind ("1280 x 720, 30 FPS, MJPG"; every rate it offers listed, once the camera has started with the machine connected), or The largest MJPG, at its fastest (none chosen), and the camera's own Properties (brightness, backlight compensation, contrast, exposure, focus, gain, gamma, hue, power line frequency, saturation, sharpness, white balance, zoom): each one ticked under Set? is set when the camera opens, and at once when changed (a slider dragged sets it as it moves, the camera running on and nothing else made again), to its Value (a slider from the camera's Min to its Max, when the camera says them, and the number) or, where the camera can, Auto (OpenPnP's Freeze Properties), in OpenPnP's columns: Auto, Min, Value, Max, Default; Min, Max and Default are the camera's own, as it reports them while it runs (kept when the camera stops, and when its panel is made again after a setting changes), and an unticked one shows the camera's value; Reapply to Camera sets them again now; Defaults, then Auto-Tune sets the camera's properties as OpenPnP's Issues & Solutions would have them for vision ("raw information from the camera sensor, even if the images look less appealing to humans"): brightness, contrast, gamma, gain, hue, saturation and white balance to the camera's own Default, sharpness to its Min, none automatic (the colour is then put right by White Balance below, as OpenPnP proposes), any other property to its Default (or left to tune itself where it can); exposure it leaves to the camera, with the camera's light on and other cameras' Anti-Glare lights off (as for a picture for vision, so the machine must be on), for at least 1.2 seconds and until its picture holds steady (a camera's automatic exposure can take seconds to come back from far off; 6 seconds at most), then switches it to manual; as many cameras do not say what their automatic exposure settled on, it is then found from the picture (a few pictures a step, each step looked at only once the camera shows it, closing in on the exposure that gives the brightness the camera gave by itself), the picture it gives then checked against that (within 15% of its brightness, at least 12 levels of 255; not tuned, and the log says what it gave, when it is not), and the values are kept, every property ticked (one step to undo), in a few seconds all told: a good starting place from which to adjust by hand. Not while a camera task is under way (its pictures would change from under it: a tip's runout measured as homing ends failed so); it says so, to be pressed again once the task has ended. Auto-Tune when homing?: each visual homing first takes the camera over the head's primary fiducial (its homing fiducial when it has none), its light on as for vision, and does Defaults, then Auto-Tune there, keeping what it arrives at; homing goes on to look for the homing fiducial once it is tuned, and fails, saying why, when it is not. Auto-Tune when calibrating?: Defaults, then Auto-Tune before every calibration that looks through the camera, where it looks, its properties kept: the camera's own calibration (over its mark, or for a camera looking up with the nozzle's tip over it), a nozzle tip's calibration over it (the tip brought to the camera's focus first), an axis's backlash (over the homing fiducial), the precise nozzle offsets (over the test object), the Feature Diameter's preview, Auto-Detect Next and its measuring, capturing a fiducial (the homing mark, the calibration rig's), and Auto Focus's Test (the tip over the camera at its Z). Once a spot: tuned where the camera already was tuned for a calibration (Auto-Detect Next clicked again, the feature then measured where it was sized), not again. For a camera looking up, the time something is over it to tune on. A camera that cannot be tuned (one without properties of its own) stops the calibration, saying so. Auto-Tune for each part?: bottom vision in a job tunes on the first part of each kind (Defaults, then Auto-Tune, the part in view), keeps what it arrived at for that part for the run, and puts it back for every later one of its kind without tuning again; a new run (not one resumed) tunes afresh. Auto-Tune for fiducial checks?: a fiducial check (a board's or panel's Fiducial Check, a job's fiducials before it places, Test Fiducial Locator) tunes once, over its first fiducial (Defaults, then Auto-Tune), and keeps that tune for the rest of the check. The camera's Auto-Tune icon (Machine) tunes it whenever you choose. Expose each picture? with its Brightness (1 to 254, 128 to begin with): each picture taken for vision (every pipeline's, visual homing's and calibration's, once the camera has settled) is taken with the exposure set first, by hand, for that brightness under the light there is then, for light that is not always the same: a picture looked at (once the camera shows its exposure, as Auto-Tune waits), the exposure scaled by how far its brightness is from the one wanted (a picture too bright to scale from, the exposure a quarter), looked at again, until within 8 levels, at most 6 exposures (each logged, at Debug); not reached (too dark even at its longest, say), the picture as near as it got is used and the log says so. It, Reapply to Camera and the Capture FPS Test work on the camera while its picture is hidden (behind this page, say), as every camera runs while the machine is on; Capture FPS and its Test: how many pictures a second the camera gives, counted over two seconds (any camera); one not ticked is left as the camera has it. Image Transforms, as OpenPnP's: Rotation (degrees counter-clockwise, the picture grown to the turned picture's bounds), Offset X and Offset Y (pixels, black where the picture moved from), Flip Vertical? (upside down) and Flip Horizontal? (left to right), Crop Width and Crop Height (0 for no cropping; cut about its middle), Scale Width and Scale Height (0 for no scaling), and De-Interlace? (a picture of two fields stacked woven back into one); done to each picture first, in OpenPnP's order (de-interlaced, cropped, scaled, turned, moved, flipped), so the camera is calibrated for the picture they give: calibrate it again after changing them. Brought in from OpenPnP unless its advanced calibration overrides them (then OpenPnP does not apply them either). White Balance: each colour's balance and gamma, applied to every picture (what you see and what vision works on), as in OpenPnP: Red Balance, Green Balance, Blue Balance, Red Gamma, Green Gamma and Blue Gamma, each a slider from 0 to 200 percent (100 leaves it as it is) with its value beside it to type; under Auto White-Balance, Overall and Brightest work them out from what the camera sees now (have something white or grey in view); Mapped Roughly (8 levels) and Mapped Finely (32) map each colour at each level of brightness, with a gradiented grey object in view (failing where there is no grey at a level), the balance and gamma then showing roughly what the map does (setting one by hand drops the map); Reset takes them off. Color Balance plots each colour's Output Level against its Input Level (one grey line when neutral), following the sliders as they move. An OpenPnP import brings the balance, the gammas and the maps. Position: the head it is on and its axes and offset, or where a fixed camera is, and for a fixed camera its Roaming Radius, as OpenPnP's: how far from the camera's centre a nozzle may carry a part at camera Z, which bounds the largest part bottom vision can see in several shots (zero: one shot only, no vision compositing); within it the nozzle moves between shots without going up to safe Z. A fixed camera's Focus Sensing Method (General Configuration), None or AutoFocus, gives it OpenPnP's Auto Focus tab: Focal Resolution (where the search stops), Averaged Frames, Focus Speed (a share of the machine's), Show Diagnostics? (each picture's sharpest edges marked in green on the camera), and the Test button (the pin): the nozzle chosen on the Jog panel, with its tip, brought over the camera from its tip's tallest part above the camera's Z down to it, and found in focus: each pass steps through the range (at most 11 steps), scores each picture by its hardest edges, and narrows to the steps beside the best, until a step is within the focal resolution. Last Focus Distance is how far above the camera's Z that was; Adjust Camera Z (the nozzle over the camera, holding no part, after a test) makes the camera's Z the nozzle's, after asking: Units per Pixel must then be calibrated again. In a job, a part of unknown height is found so before bottom vision (over each of its shots, the average), and its height kept; without auto focus, a part of unknown height fails, as in OpenPnP. Advanced Calibration: General Settings, as OpenPnP's: Deinterlace, Cropped Width and Cropped Height (the same as Image Transforms'), and Default Working Plane Z: for a camera on a head, the height of what it looks at when that is not known otherwise (typically the boards' surface; until set, the height it was calibrated at), where its scale is taken once calibrated at two heights; for a fixed camera, its own Z (the height parts' bottoms are lowered to for alignment, as on Position); Start Calibration; its Pipeline, OpenPnP's Advanced Calibration pipeline that finds the calibration mark in each picture (OpenPnP's: ImageCapture, DetectCircularSymmetry and ConvertModelToKeyPoints; the expected centre, distance and diameter set as its DetectCircularSymmetry properties, the mark its results keypoint): Edit Pipeline opens it in the pipeline editor on the camera's picture, and Reset Pipeline puts OpenPnP's default back; an OpenPnP import brings the camera's own; how it measures (the grid's Places Across and Places Down, 3 to 25 each; Reach, how far towards the picture's edge the grid goes, 1 as far as leaves room for the mark; Outlier Limit, how many times the fit's spread a measurement may be off before it is left out, one in ten at most; Worst Fit Taken, the spread in pixels beyond which the calibration is refused; Lead-in, each place come to from that far back along both axes, so the drives' play is taken up alike every time (1 mm to begin with), and Pictures Each, each place found in that many pictures and their mean taken (4 to begin with); Two Heights?, measuring it again at a second height: a head camera over the head's secondary calibration mark, a fixed camera with the nozzle's tip raised by Raise For The Second, 2 mm to begin with); how much of a straightened picture's bent edge shows; and for each picture size it was calibrated at, its Results: when and at what Z, units per pixel each way, the estimated locating accuracy, the field of view in mm, how far the camera is turned (and mirrored), the lens, how many measurements were made, left out and missed; measured at two heights, the second height's scale, where the camera's centre of projection is, its focal length, its field of view as angles, and how much the scale grows per mm nearer; with where the picture's middle looked measured at both heights, OpenPnP's Camera Mounting Error [Deg] about the machine's X Axis, Y Axis (how far the camera is tipped from looking straight along Z, right hand rule) and Z Axis (how far it is turned); and Calibrated Head Offsets (a camera on a head) or Camera Location (a fixed one): where the middle of the picture looks at the Default Working Plane Z against where the camera's offsets or place say. A tipped camera sees what is higher or lower a little to the side: that lean is applied wherever its scale is taken at the Default Working Plane Z; for a camera on the head, the part at the calibration height is what visual homing and the nozzle offsets were measured by, and stays; for a fixed camera, as OpenPnP applies its calibration to the machine, where the middle of its picture looked becomes its location (a Machine Setup step, to undo; worked out from wherever the tip was jogged to before measuring, not from where the camera's location said), so it is only as true as the offset of the nozzle that held its tip over it (the first nozzle on the head: calibrate the nozzle offsets first); and three graphs (below) Actuator Configuration: Properties (driver, name), Coordinate System (head), Machine Coordination (as OpenPnP's: Before Actuation?, None, CommandStillstand (the moving controllers told to finish their moves first) or WaitForStillstand (waited for to stand still), to begin with; After Actuation?, None or WaitForUnconditionalCoordination (every controller waited for and its position read); Before Read?, None or WaitForStillstand; with continuous motion off every move is waited for anyway), General (Actuation: what it is switched to once connected, once homed and before a disconnect you ask for, ActuateOn, ActuateOff or left as it is; index, unit read; Value Type: Boolean, Double, String or Profile), Commands (on, off; for a Double or String one, Set Value, {value} replaced by the value, and the On / Off Values that On and Off set it to when they have no commands of their own; read, reply pattern: the value its (?<Value>...) group finds in the reply, as OpenPnP's Actuator Read Regex, else its first group). Profiles, for a Profile actuator, as OpenPnP's actuator profiles: Actuator 1 to Actuator 6, the actuators it sets, and its profiles, each a Name, Default ON and Default OFF (one profile each, and a profile not both) and a value for each actuator (true or false for a switch, a profile for another profile actuator, else as typed; empty leaves it as it is), with Delete and Add Profile. Set to a profile's name, each actuator is set to its value; switched on or off, it takes the Default ON or OFF profile. An actuator a profile sets cannot be removed. New with Actuators chosen asks which kind: ReferenceActuator, driven by a controller's commands, OpenPnP's NeoDen4FeederActuator (see A NeoDen 4 above), OpenPnP's ThermistorToLinearSensorActuator, with a Transforms tab: what it reads is taken as a temperature (degrees C) and given as what a linear sensor in its place would read, the resistance a thermistor with the Steinhart-Hart coefficients A, B and C has at it (100 kOhm at 25 degrees C to begin with), read below R2 (4700) in a divider by an ADC of Maximum Value (4095) and Voltage Reference (3.3), as a voltage, times Scale plus Offset (R1, as in OpenPnP, is not yet supported), OpenPnP's ScriptActuator, with a Script group naming the Script Name, a script of the scripts folder (see the Scripts menu) run to actuate it, told actuateBoolean when switched, actuateDouble (a Double one) or actuateString when set, and its own name as actuator, or OpenPnP's HttpActuator, with an HTTP group in place of the commands: switched by a GET of its On URL or Off URL (with none, the Param URL with 1 or 0), set by the Param URL with {val} the value, read by its Read URL (its answer's lines, or each one's (?<Value>...) group of the Read Regex); a URL the same as the one asked last is not asked again. Axis Interlock? (in Coordinate System) gives it OpenPnP's Axis Interlock tab: an Interlock Type and up to four axes (Axis 1 to Axis 4). When one of them moves, a Signal type switches the actuator: on while they move (SignalAxesMoving) or stand still, inside or outside their safe zone, parked or not (switched before the move when that is being left, after it when it is being come to); a Confirm type reads it before or after the move, a number that must be within the Confirmation range or text that must match the Confirmation pattern (Regex? for a regular expression), and stops the machine with what it read otherwise. Interlock Conditions: only while a Boolean Actuator is in its state (Just: and changed since; Unknown: or never switched), and at a machine Speed [%] in range

A camera's calibration results end in three graphs of its measurements, each measurement's residual being how far from where the fit puts it the mark was seen. Residual Errors in the Order Measured shows them along X and Y, one after another: they should look like noise about zero, and a step or a drift says something moved while measuring (the mark, the camera in its mount, a missed step, a slipping belt). Residual Errors, X against Y shows them all together, with the outlier limit as a circle: one round cluster about the middle is right; two clusters, or a stretched one, say the mark was found badly or the backlash or a drive is out. The Residual Error Map colours the picture by how far off the measurements near each place are, coolest to hottest; it shows where, not how much, and should look patchy at random: rings or stripes mean the lens fits the picture badly there. A calibration made before the graphs were kept shows its results without them until it is calibrated again.

A nozzle tip's runout is how its end swings round as the nozzle turns: an end not quite on the nozzle's axis. The tip's Calibration tab is laid out as OpenPnP's: a Calibration group (Enable?, with the Position Tool button beside it; Calibrate and Reset; Auto Recalibration; Fail Homing?, shown only for the recalibrations on homing, MachineHome and NozzleTipChange), then Nozzle Tip Calibration (Status, the tip on the nozzle it is on and its runout there, or "Uncalibrated", or "Please load the nozzle tip on a nozzle."; the measuring settings below), then Background Calibration. As OpenPnP's, with Enable? off everything else on the tab is greyed; with Method None, the background's settings are; with Brightness, its Hue and Saturation tolerances; the ranges found are shown, not edited. Calibrate measures the tip at once, as OpenPnP's (nothing asked), on the nozzle it is on (the Jog panel's tip menu has Calibrate too), with the fixed camera looking up (as OpenPnP's, never while the nozzle holds a part: "Cannot calibrate nozzle tip with part on nozzle N1.", and not after homing either; a part jplacer was not told of, such as one still on a nozzle when jplacer was started, it cannot know about): the nozzle over the camera, down to its focus plus the Calibration Z Offset, turned to each of Circle Divisions angles round the circle (up to Allowed Misdectects, OpenPnP's spelling, of them may fail), its end found at each (Vision Diameter across; 0: the tip's diameter; each find shown on the camera, a green circle and cross where it was, as the camera's own calibration shows its), and fitted as its Compensation Algorithm says (OpenPnP's, which keeps it in its machine.xml; ModelCameraOffsetAffine for a new tip, as OpenPnP's default; a tip kept before there was a choice keeps how it was compensated, ModelNoOffset). As OpenPnP's, an end found further than the Offset Threshold from where the nozzle was sent counts as a misdetect (it is looked for that far and 40% more); too many, and the calibration fails with OpenPnP's words. Position Tool takes the nozzle the tip is on over the camera looking up, at its focus plus the Calibration Z Offset (where the camera is for that nozzle, below).

The algorithms, as OpenPnP's: Model, ModelNoOffset and ModelCameraOffset fit a circle by the Kasa method, the phase the average of each angle less where the end was found about its centre; their Affine ones fit the affine transform taking where an end of 1 mm runout would be onto where it was found (its translation the centre, its scales the runout, its rotation the phase), which copes better with noise; Table keeps the measurements themselves. With Enable? on, every move of that nozzle is sent the compensation the other way, and a turn alone moves X and Y to keep the end where it is: a Model the whole offset (the swing, and the axis's offset from where the camera's position and the nozzle's offset say, taken as the nozzle's offset being off), a NoOffset or CameraOffset the swing alone, a Table its offsets, in proportion between their angles. With a CameraOffset one, the camera looking up is taken to be off by the axis's offset for that nozzle: the nozzle goes over it there for bottom vision, Position Tool and Move Selected Nozzle to Camera. The results show the algorithm, the runout (the circle's radius, and the angle it points at), the axis's offset (Center, Camera Position Error for a NoOffset one, Camera Position Offset for a CameraOffset one; a Table's First Offset), how well the circle fits, and a graph of each measurement about the axis. Each nozzle the tip was measured on keeps its own; Reset forgets it for the nozzle it is on. An OpenPnP import brings how it is measured (whether compensated, the algorithm, migrated as OpenPnP does for an older one, the divisions, the misdetects allowed, the offset threshold, the Z offset, when it is measured again) and what OpenPnP measured on each nozzle; importing again keeps what jplacer measured over it, and the tip's own pipeline. The tip is found in each picture by its Pipeline, as OpenPnP's (ImageCapture, DetectCircularSymmetry under the nozzleTip properties, given where to look, how far and the Vision Diameter; one result within the offset threshold, more than one not taken), on the camera's picture in colour and straightened, as OpenPnP's pipelines are given it: Edit opens it in the pipeline editor on the camera looking up, and Reset puts the default back (OpenPnP's, its circle found to an eighth of a pixel, super-sampling 8, where OpenPnP's own default finds it to the whole pixel).

OpenPnP's Calibrate Camera Position and Rotation is not on the tab: OpenPnP hides it once the camera looking up has Advanced Calibration, as every jplacer camera has. The camera looking up's own Calibrate (see Machine) does it, with this tip over it, after its runout: it sends the tip, its runout compensated, round a circle over the camera looking up, its Excenter Ratio (a quarter, to begin with; brought from OpenPnP) of the picture's smaller side out from the middle, turning with it, and finds it at each of the Circle Divisions angles, with the Offset Threshold about where it was sent. For an Affine algorithm, the affine transform taking where it was seen onto where it was sent gives where the camera is (its translation) and how far it is turned; for the others, the circle through what was seen (its centre how far the camera is off, its phase the turn, less the excenter's own direction, which OpenPnP's leaves in). The camera's place is set to it, and its turn put right in its calibrations (with none, OpenPnP's way: its picture's rotation). With a CameraOffset algorithm the axis's own offset is taken to be the camera's, so the place found is where the camera is for that nozzle.

Auto Recalibration, as OpenPnP's, says when it is measured again without asking: NozzleTipChange (on each load of the tip, by the changer or by hand with Manual Change, and once the machine is homed), NozzleTipChangeInJob (forgotten on each load; a job measures it before the nozzle's first pick), MachineHome (once homed, and on a load when not yet measured on that nozzle) or Manual. A load while the machine is not homed is measured once it is homed. A load a running job makes is measured by the job itself, in its Calibrate Nozzle Tip step before the nozzle's next pick, and not again beside it. A tip is never measured with a part on its nozzle: a part jplacer takes to be on it (one let go by hand, the vacuum switched off on the Actuators panel, is still taken to be there) is discarded first, as the Jog panel's Discard does, and the tip then measured; a tip change forgets the part, which went with the tip. The precise offsets calibration and Check Placement discard such a part first too, and Check Placement measures the tip's runout first when it has none on that nozzle. However it is measured, the camera shows each find as it comes: the picture with a green circle and cross where the tip was found and the size it was found, and which turn of how many, so a wrong find shows at once. Once homed, a tip set to NozzleTipChange or MachineHome is measured on the nozzle it is on (after visual homing, before Machine.AfterHoming and the park), and forgotten on the nozzles it fits but is not on; with Fail Homing?, a measurement failing then leaves the machine not homed ("Homing failed", in a dialog with the reason). Without it, homing goes on and a dialog, "Nozzle tip not calibrated", gives the reason: the tip's runout is not compensated until it is calibrated (its Calibrate) or the machine is homed again. A job measures any tip it uses that is to be compensated and not yet measured on its nozzle (Calibrate nozzle tip, before the picks). One that fails pauses the run, whatever the placements' Error Handling ("Nozzle tip ... was not calibrated: ...", in the Job Error dialog): no placement is put in error, and Resume or Step measures it again, the run going on only once it is calibrated.

Loaded? on a nozzle's Nozzle Tips tab says which tip is on it now: ticking one moves nothing, and a tip is on one nozzle at a time.

docs.title: Places
docs.text:
A place (a homing fiducial, a park location, a fixed camera's location, where a changer step goes) is one row of coordinates ending in four buttons:

  • Capture Camera and Capture Nozzle set it from where the camera on the head, or the nozzle chosen on the Jog panel, is now: one step to undo.
  • Move Camera and Move Nozzle go there: up to safe Z, across, and down to the Z given. A camera's Z (usually a virtual one, which moves nothing) says the height it looks at, so the reticle and footprints are drawn at the scale there; a camera with no Z stays as it is. The machine must be connected and homed; the speed is the Jog panel's. While a calibration, a nozzle tip change or a running job is moving the machine, the move is refused ("Not moved: …"), not slipped in between the task's own moves; a calibration waiting for you (to jog the tip into the circle, say) leaves the moves to you.

Where OpenPnP has them, two more follow:

  • Position Tool (Without Safe Z), on a motion test's stops: the nozzle goes there straight, without going up to safe Z first. A nozzle tip's loading or unloading move has none: its Move Nozzle goes as the step is set, by way of safe Z only with Safe Z?, compensated for backlash only with Backlash?.
  • Contact Probe Tool, on a tool changer's Touch Location: as OpenPnP's, after asking (it overwrites the Z reference, so places captured before must be captured again), the default probing nozzle (the first that probes by contact), its Z calibration forgotten, goes over the place at its Z plus the probe's Start Offset by way of safe Z, probes down as far as its Depth, goes back up, and the Z it met is put in the place: one step to undo.

A soft limit or safe zone end has the same two kinds of button for its axis: set it from where the axis is, or move the axis there.

Only what jplacer acts on is shown. Whatever else a cell carries (brought from OpenPnP for features not built yet) is kept as it is. A camera's calibrations are measured, not set here (see Cameras); the machine's squareness comes from OpenPnP (see Importing from OpenPnP).

Putting a part on a head gives it the head's X and Y axes, as its other parts have; taking it off one clears its axes.

docs.title: A nozzle tip's changer
docs.text:
No two machines change tips the same way: from trays at the side, from the back, through a door that opens, with a lock to release, or by hand. So a tip's changer is not described, it is taught: a list of steps on the tip's Tool Changer tab (one table for loading, one for unloading of its own; the steps are not in the tree), run in order, built from

  • move: the nozzle doing the change goes to X, Y, Z and a rotation, at a speed (a share of top speed). One left empty stays as it is (a move giving only Z goes straight up or down). Safe Z?: up to safe Z, across, then down to its Z; without, straight there, every axis at once. Backlash?: compensated as every other move is; without, it goes without the backlash compensation that goes past the place and back (one-sided's, sneaking up's, the distance-aware back-off), which among the slots would carry the tip into a slot's wall. Its Move Nozzle moves the nozzle as the step is set.
  • safe Z: the nozzle up to safe Z.
  • actuator: switch one on or off (a door, a lock, a valve).
  • wait: a number of milliseconds.
  • ask: a message for you, to carry on or cancel (a tip put on by hand, a door to open).

The first step is a move giving X, Y and Z, by way of Safe Z (the nozzle may be anywhere when a change begins; the tip shows a problem until it is), and loading ends at safe Z. A first step added starts with Safe Z? ticked; every move starts with Backlash? off. Steps saved before these choices came in as they ran: the first move by way of safe Z, the others straight, none compensated. A tip with no steps is put on by hand.

A move's place is where the nozzle goes, not the camera: the nozzle's offset on the head is taken care of. It is in the axes' own coordinates, before the machine's squareness correction, so changing the squareness never moves it: up to a few tenths of a millimetre at the far end of the machine, enough to miss a slot.

Each row's buttons add a step after it, delete it, or move it up or down.

Unloading is loading run backwards unless the tip is set to steps of its own: in by way of safe Z to where loading ended, then each move goes back to where the move before it went as the move it undoes went (its speed, Safe Z? and Backlash?); an actuator is switched the other way; a move that came down from a safe Z step is undone by going up, then across. The steps it works out are listed under Unloading, to check; to change them, change loading, or choose steps of its own, which start as those.

docs.title: Changes are used as you make them
docs.text:
There is no Apply: each change goes to the running machine, and is saved in the cell file, as you make it. A value in a field is changed when you press Return or Tab or leave the field, or step a number up or down; until then only the field has changed, and Escape puts back the value it had. A box ticked or a choice made is changed at once.

Nothing is disconnected: the controllers take their new settings as they run, and the machine stays homed. A controller's connection settings (its port, speed or flow control, its firmware profile, how long it waits while connecting) are used the next time you connect; a controller added is connected then too. After a change to the axes the machine must be homed again, as its coordinates then mean something else.

What is wrong with the setup (a part naming one that is not there) is listed under the settings, and nothing is handed to the machine until it is put right: the machine keeps the setup it had.

While the machine is moving, changes wait for it to stop. A change to a camera, a head or an axis also waits while a camera task is under way (a calibration, a tip's runout measured as homing ends, visual homing), until it has ended ("Machine Setup's changes are taken once the camera task under way ends"): made at once, it would make the cameras again and lose what the task found. Calibrations and squareness measured while the setup was being changed are kept. The camera panels are made again only when a camera, a head or an axis changed, each in its dock where you left it (floating in a window of its own, or docked among the tabs); a camera renamed gets a new one, in the cameras' place.

docs.title: Undo and Redo
docs.text: Edit ▸ Undo (Ctrl+Z) and Edit ▸ Redo (Ctrl+Y) step back and forward through Machine Setup's changes (and the library's, the last made first: see Parts), the machine following; each says what it would undo or redo ("Undo Add Camera"), and takes you to where the change was made. What was measured (a camera's calibration, the squareness) is not undone. Changes one after another to the same setting (a number stepped up several times) are one step. The steps are kept until another cell is opened.

docs.title: Machine
docs.text:
jplacer drives a machine through a cell: one machine's description, kept in a cell file. It lists the machine's controllers and how jplacer reaches them, its axes, its head with the nozzles, cameras and actuators on it, and anything fixed to the machine itself. The cell you opened last is opened again when jplacer starts.

Cell files live in cells/ in jplacer's configuration folder (~/.config/jplacer/cells on Linux).

docs.title: The first start
docs.text:
As OpenPnP does, jplacer started with no machine yet brings in OpenPnP's own default machine: a simulated controller, one nozzle, a camera looking down at OpenPnP's test picture of the table (pnp-test.png) and one looking up, and the strip feeders laid out on that picture. Configuration files not there yet (packages, parts, vision settings) start as OpenPnP's defaults too. Both travel with jplacer, as does the picture: a machine.xml naming one of OpenPnP's own pictures (classpath://samples/…) is given that copy. OpenPnP's sample job, pnp-test.job.xml with its board and panel, is put in the samples/pnp-test folder beside jplacer's settings (~/.config/jplacer), to open with File ▸ Open Job…. The machine's cameras work as OpenPnP's do with no calibration here: an ImageCamera, or a SimulatedUpCamera (which shows the nozzle tip and the part on it, its body dark and its pads white, as the part is turned), at its Units Per Pixel. A machine with no discard location has it at the origin, as OpenPnP's default.

The default machine is only brought in when there is no machine at all. With the settings not naming one but machines already kept beside them (cells), jplacer opens the one changed last instead, and never writes OpenPnP's default over one. Saving the settings never takes anything out of the file: every setting it has is kept, and only what this run changed is written (a setting put back to its default is the one thing taken out). A settings file that cannot be read is left exactly as it is, and nothing is written to it that run. The settings are written whole or not at all, and kept before an update starts the new version, so the new version always finds them.

docs.title: Bringing in a machine set up in OpenPnP
docs.text:
If your machine already runs under OpenPnP, Machine ▸ Import OpenPnP Machine… reads OpenPnP's machine.xml and makes a cell from it, so you do not set the machine up a second time. When OpenPnP's file is where OpenPnP keeps it (.openpnp2/machine.xml in your home folder), jplacer asks whether to import that one: Import, or Choose Another File… to pick a different machine.xml. In the file dialog, tick Show hidden (or press Ctrl+H) to see folders whose names start with a dot, such as .openpnp2. The new cell is saved as cells/openpnp.json and opened straight away. Importing again replaces that file, except for what was set, taught or measured here, which is kept: the port each controller was set to, each camera's calibrations and how much of a straightened picture it shows, the squareness correction, each nozzle tip's loading and unloading steps, and which tip is on each nozzle (OpenPnP's file says what it last believed; a hand may have changed it since).

What is brought across:

  • Controllers that OpenPnP talks G-code to, with their serial port settings (port, speed, flow control, parity, data and stop bits, DTR / RTS, line endings), their maximum feed rate and G-code logging. An actuator with no controller of its own, or naming one the machine does not have, is the first controller's, as in OpenPnP. A G-code controller OpenPnP simulates (Communications simulated, or TCP to the address GcodeServer) is simulated here as OpenPnP does it: by its GcodeServer (see Simulation Mode in Machine Setup). A linear transform axis brings its inputs and factors (OpenPnP writes them input-axis-X-id, factor-x, ...), so a non-squareness transform becomes the squareness correction. OpenPnP's NullDriver (its simulated controller) becomes jplacer's simulated one, a grblHAL: its axes given the letters a grblHAL of that many axes has (the first of X, Y, Z, A, B, C, U, V), X and Y by type, the rotations A, B, C, a Z the Z, the rest what is left (two nozzles: Z, A, B and C). An old machine.xml whose one controller is a <driver> NullDriver (OpenPnP's own default machine still is) is first brought up to date as OpenPnP does on loading it: an X and a Y axis for all, a Z and a rotation axis of its own for each nozzle (the rotation limited as the nozzle was, its old Safe Z the axis's safe zone), virtual ones for each camera, at the old feed rate (rotation ten times it) reached in half a second, and the head's homing fiducial at 5.736, 6.112 (the lower left fiducial of OpenPnP's test picture).
  • Axes: those driven by a controller, those with no hardware behind them (such as a camera's Z), and those that follow another axis (such as two nozzles sharing one Z, one of them reversed).
  • The head, its nozzles (with the actuator for each nozzle's vacuum, the nozzle tips that fit it and the one on it; a nozzle from an older OpenPnP naming only its vacuum actuator, or only its vacuum sense actuator, uses that one for both, as OpenPnP does on loading it), cameras (each by the name its device gives itself, with its light; an OpenCvCamera by its device index, /dev/video<index>, its OpenCV capture properties as the camera's settings; a Webcam by its name; MJPG, image, switcher, ONVIF and GStreamer cameras as they were; a SimulatedUpCamera as a simulated camera that sees the nozzle tips in Simulation Mode) and actuators, and the cameras and actuators fixed to the machine.
  • Actuator commands: how each one is switched on and off, and how a value is read from it.
  • The home command, every line of it, in order: a machine's homing sequence (release Z, home Y and X onto their switches, set the coordinates, home Z…) is the controller's own, and Home runs it.
  • The connect wait: how long to listen after opening the port before asking anything.
  • Each camera's settings (exposure, white balance, gain, focus, brightness, contrast and so on, set or automatic), which jplacer sets again every time it opens the camera: a camera that dropped off its connection comes back as it was, not on its own defaults.
  • Non-squareness: a machine squared in OpenPnP (its X axis a linear transform adding a share of Y) keeps that correction, as jplacer's squareness. Any other linear transform axis comes in as a linear axis, its inputs, factors and offset as they were.
  • Nozzle tips: each one's name, the diameter OpenPnP's nozzle tip calibration finds it by, as the diameter the camera looking up sees, and its tool changer: its places (start, middle, second middle, end, those set) and speeds, and the actuators switched between them, become the tip's load steps, unloading being loading backwards as in OpenPnP. A tip a nozzle's list still names after it was deleted in OpenPnP is left out.
  • Vision: the bottom vision's settings (on or off, the vision settings parts use by default, passes) and the fiducial locator's (its vision settings, its tolerances), and the job processor's settings (see Job Processors).
  • The head's places: its homing fiducial and whether it homes visually, its park location (none set in OpenPnP: the origin, where OpenPnP parks it), the calibration rig's two fiducials (their places, heights and diameters) and test object, and its pump (which actuator, when it runs, how long it takes to come up).

When the import finishes, a message says what was brought in and lists anything to check: a part of the OpenPnP set-up jplacer has no equivalent for yet (some axis types, a controller that is not G-code or is reached over the network), or a command that uses something jplacer cannot fill in yet. Those parts are left out or kept exactly as OpenPnP wrote them.

The machine's feeders are brought across too, onto the Feeders tab, each exactly as OpenPnP wrote it; they take the place of the feeders jplacer had. OpenPnP names a feeder's part (and a slot bank's, and a drop box's dummy part) by OpenPnP's ID for it, which is the library part's Name in jplacer: each is linked to the library's part of that name. Parts and packages are not imported (copy OpenPnP's parts.xml and packages.xml into jplacer's configuration folder: the library takes those it lacks), and neither is OpenPnP's camera calibration: jplacer measures its cameras itself, and the import notes each camera that had one.

docs.title: Opening a cell
docs.text: Machine ▸ Open Cell… opens a cell file you choose.

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text:
Two icons at the left of the toolbar show the machine's state at a glance, and are clicked to change it: the chip for the connection and the house for homing. Each sits in a ring: grey when idle, an amber arc while it is working, green when done, red with a break when the last attempt failed. Hover over one to see what it means now.

Clicking the chip (or Machine ▸ Connect) connects to every controller in the cell. For each one jplacer:

  1. opens its port, and listens for a moment (one second unless the cell says otherwise; an imported machine keeps OpenPnP's connect wait) so a board that greets a new connection has finished before it is asked anything;
  2. asks it what firmware it runs, and picks the matching firmware profile (grblHAL, Grbl, or a generic G-code profile when it does not recognise the answer), noting any plugins the firmware reports;
  3. sends the profile's start-up command, unless the controller reports it is in alarm (Grbl after a reset mid-move, an emergency stop, or a limit switch hit). A controller in alarm refuses G-code until it is unlocked, so it is connected all the same, the red ALARM strip shows, and the start-up command waits for Home;
  4. reads the settings the controller stores itself, where the profile says how.

If any controller fails, the others are disconnected again and the panel says why. A port where nothing answers is a failure, not a connection: it is the wrong port, or the controller is off. A port another program has open is refused ("in use by another program"): two programs on one port would each get part of what the controller says. Close the other program (OpenPnP, another jplacer, a terminal) first. Disconnect closes every connection.

When a connection fails, the chip turns red and the status bar at the bottom of the window says why. If a connection is lost while working (a cable pulled, the controller reset), a red CONNECTION LOST strip runs across the top of the window until you connect again: that strip is kept for what must not be missed. In order, most pressing first: ALARM (a controller stopped on an alarm), CONNECTION LOST, FAILED (a camera task, such as a calibration or the precise nozzle offsets, that failed: what and why, until the next task starts) and WAITING (a wait on purpose while it lasts, such as the pump coming up to pressure for its Pump On Wait).

What fails with nothing waiting on it is said in a Machine dialog, with why, and in the log: a nozzle tip's Calibrate now, the Jog panel's Pick and Place, Detect Firmware, an error a controller sends unasked, a controller reset mid-move, a connection lost. The same words are not opened again while their dialog is showing.

docs.title: Choosing the port
docs.text: USB serial ports are numbered in the order devices happen to start (ttyACM0, ttyACM1, …), so the number a controller had yesterday — or in OpenPnP's configuration — can belong to a different device today. For each controller on a serial port, its Machine Setup page has a Port list showing the serial devices plugged in now, by the name each device gives itself. Choosing one saves it in the cell, using the device's permanent name (under /dev/serial/by-id on Linux), which stays the same whatever order devices start in. While connected, the connection stays as it is: the port chosen is used the next time you connect (see Changes are used as you make them); Undo takes the choice back. A port the cell names but that is not plugged in is listed as "(not found)".

docs.title: Firmware profiles
docs.text: A firmware profile is a small file describing one kind of controller firmware: how to recognise it, the commands it takes, how it replies, how it reports its position, and how its stored settings are read. jplacer comes with profiles for grblHAL (including the JayTEK plugin's vacuum and analog readings), Grbl 1.1, and generic G-code; and, as OpenPnP sets them up, for Smoothieware, Marlin, RepRapFirmware (Duet) and TinyG: each known by its answer to M115 (its FIRMWARE_NAME), its position read with M114, moves waited for with M400 (TinyG: its own ok and err: replies, G28.2 to home, G28.3 to set its place). On a controller whose profile reads no position (generic G-code), the axes are where they were last sent once a move is waited for, as OpenPnP's drivers keep them. A profile of your own, placed in profiles/ in jplacer's configuration folder, is used as well, and replaces a bundled one with the same id.

docs.title: The machine's panels
docs.text:
While a cell is open, its panels sit in docks:

  • the cameras top left, tabbed together;
  • under them the machine controls, Jog and Actuators;
  • the rest of the window, tabbed: Machine Setup and Machine;
  • the Console across the bottom.

Every split between them can be dragged, as far as leaves the panels in the middle room for themselves. Each is a dock like any other: drag its tab to another place, tear it out into a window of its own, or stack it with others.

View has a tick for each panel. Untick one to close it (or close it with its tab's ×); tick it to bring it back, where it lives above, in front of the others there.

jplacer opens as it was last closed: the window's place and size (or maximized), every panel where you left it (docked, tabbed, split, or in a window of its own, at its place and size), the tab in front of each group, the splits' sizes, and the panels closed staying closed. A panel new since then (a camera added) goes to its place above.

docs.title: Where the tool is
docs.text: The right of the status bar says where the tool chosen in Jog is: X, Y, Z and C (its rotation), as Jog's boxes have them, in green. Click it to measure: it reads Relative, in blue, counting from where the tool was at that moment, so jogging to a second place reads the distance between the two. Click it again to go back to where the tool is.

docs.title: A controller's firmware and state
docs.text: Each controller's Machine Setup page shows, under Firmware, what firmware it said it runs and its State: what it says it is doing now (Idle, Run, Hold, Alarm…), or not connected, kept up to date while the page is shown. Whether the machine is connected and homed shows on the toolbar's connect and home buttons and in the strip across the window; what it has been measured for, on each part's own page (a camera's calibration, the squareness, the head's homing).

docs.title: Homing
docs.text:
Clicking the house (or Machine ▸ Home All Axes) sends each controller its home command and waits for it to finish (a controller in alarm is first sent the profile's unlock, $X on Grbl, and the start-up command it missed: homing is what makes its position known again), then tells the controller that every axis is at its home coordinate. Until the machine is homed it will not move: before that its position means nothing, so its soft limits cannot protect it. A machine imported from OpenPnP homes the way it did in OpenPnP, with the same command.

The switches put the head within a fraction of a millimetre. Where the head is set to home visually (an imported head that did so in OpenPnP is), Home then finishes with the camera: the calibrated camera on the head is brought to the front, looks at the homing mark, and the coordinates are corrected so the mark measures exactly where the head's settings say it is (the homing part's footprint drawn on the camera while it looks). The homing part is the head's Homing Fiducial Part in Machine Setup, chosen from the library's parts; a machine set up before there was the choice uses its part named FIDUCIAL-HOME (OpenPnP's), shown there as the one chosen. As OpenPnP's, it looks again, up to the homing part's fiducial vision settings' Max Vision Passes (3 to begin with), until a look corrects it by less than their Max Linear Offset (0.2 mm to begin with); the last look's correction stands. With the camera's Auto-Tune when homing? ticked, the camera is first tuned over the head's primary fiducial (see Machine Setup). The status bar (and the log) says by how much it corrected. Until a camera on the head is calibrated, Home says it homed by the switches only. Should visual homing fail (the mark not found, the camera not tuned), the homing has failed, as OpenPnP's: the machine is not homed (its coordinates are the switches', which the mark did not confirm), Home turns red, and the status bar says why; the tips' recalibration, Machine.AfterHoming and the park do not follow.

The house is grey while the machine is not homed, an amber arc while it homes (the whole homing: the switches, visual homing, the tips' recalibration and Machine.AfterHoming), and green once homed; a failed home turns it red and the status bar says why. A red ALARM strip runs across the top of the window when a controller has stopped on an alarm.

docs.title: Parking
docs.text:
Machine ▸ Park Head (once the machine is homed) takes the head out of the way: every Z axis on the head comes up into its safe zone first, then the head goes to its park place (an imported head keeps OpenPnP's), placed by its camera. A park place past a soft limit (often one is set right at the end of travel) is gone to as near as the limit allows. It moves at half speed.

Once parked in X and Y (not a Z or rotation park), every camera's light is switched off, on screen or not, and kept off until you next do something at a camera: a move to it (a jog, Position Tool, Move Selected Nozzle to Camera, a click in its picture) or its light switched on by hand. A camera taking a picture for vision still lights itself for it, as its Light settings say.

docs.title: Backlash
docs.text:
Every drive has a little play (backlash): an axis stops in a slightly different place depending on which way it was travelling. Each axis has a compensation method (its Backlash Compensation tab in Machine Setup):

Method None Where the play leaves it. OneSidedPositioning Every move ends the same way: to its target plus the offset first (its sign says which side), then in to the target at the speed factor, so the last stretch is always the same. The offset need only be at least the play. OneSidedOptimizedPositioning As OneSidedPositioning, but a move already arriving the right way goes straight in: fewer moves, its last stretch as long as the move. DirectionalCompensation A move travelling the way the offset points goes the offset further, taking up the play; the other way, it goes to the target. The offset must be the play itself. DirectionalSneakUp As DirectionalCompensation, the last Sneak-up Distance of each move made at the speed factor, so it cannot overshoot. DistanceAware jplacer's own, for a drive whose play keeps growing the further it goes (a gap taken up first, then a belt winding up). Calibrate measures the lag behind where the drive is sent against the distance travelled from fully wound the other way. jplacer keeps each drive's lag as it goes: a move starts from wherever the lag is on that curve (a short move the other way leaves it partly wound) and goes on along it by how far the drive travels, and is sent the lag it will have on arriving. A move that would come in less than the Least Approach along the curve (where the gap is taken up) first backs off that far, then comes in at the speed factor.

With a directional offset taken up, the position shown is the axis's own, without the offset. An imported machine keeps OpenPnP's method, offset, sneak-up distance and speed factor. Changing an axis's backlash, speed or limits leaves the machine homed: only a change to where an axis is (its kind, controller, letter, home coordinate or mapping) needs it homed again. Such a change does what the machine no longer being homed does anywhere: a homing still finishing (visual homing) ends, the house goes grey and Home can be clicked, and vision strip and blinds feeders drop their calibrations.

A nozzle tip changer's move without Backlash? (its tip's Tool Changer tab) makes no extra backlash moves: no going past a place and back (one-sided), no stopping short to sneak up, no distance-aware back-off; a directional offset still shifts where it ends. Among the slots, a one-sided axis would carry the tip its offset past a slot's point, into its wall. A move with Backlash? is compensated as any other.

The Jog panel's Backlash Compensation (under the pad) turns every axis's compensation off, or on again, for every move from then on: a jog, a place button, a job, a tip change. It is ticked each time jplacer starts. With Backlash Off Below Safe Z (the Safety tab, ticked to begin with, kept for next time) a jog made while a Z of a tool on the head is below its safe Z (where it was sent, not where its motor stopped: an axis stops on its nearest step, so one sent to safe Z may read a fraction of a step below it) goes straight to its place, nothing past it and back; it is decided as each jog is sent, and no other move is touched (a job's, a camera task's, a place button's, the move after going up: each compensated). Meanwhile the box is shown greyed. Each axis's Backlash Compensation tab says under its method whether compensation is on now (Compensation Now), and when it is off, why: unticked on the Jog panel, or backlash being calibrated.

Calibrate on an X or Y axis's Backlash Compensation tab measures its play with the camera that rides on it, over the head's homing fiducial (the machine homed, the camera calibrated), compensation off while it measures:

It does as OpenPnP's backlash calibration does, with its figures. The tolerance is the axis's resolution taken to at least 0.01 mm, or a quarter of a pixel when that is coarser. Each measurement is the mean of 8 pictures.

  1. Speed control: the axis timed over 10 mm at each speed factor (25, 33, 50, 75 and 100%); one that moves no slower at 25% (the controller ignoring the feed rate) stops the calibration, saying so.
  2. A step test over a millimetre: each step, from a millimetre before it, must land where it was sent, else it stops (the camera's scale, or the mark's height, is wrong).
  3. The backlash coming in from distances, each the last times the square root of 2, up to 10 mm, and the full range (to the soft limit): from each side, from where it stands and wound from 90 mm that side first, the last of it at the slowest speed. The largest backlash coming in from up to 2.5 mm, and the shortest of those distances still showing it (to within twice the tolerance), give the sneak-up distance (the larger of the two).
  4. The offset at each speed factor: compensated, in to the mark from 90 mm either side, the offset corrected by 90% of what is left, up to 4 times or until the two agree within the tolerance.
  5. The method, by OpenPnP's rules: a sneak-up distance longer than 0.8 mm (the play keeps growing with how far the axis came in, as a stretching belt does): OneSidedPositioning, its offset that largest backlash. Otherwise, when the offset found is less than the sneak-up distance needs: DirectionalSneakUp, its offset halfway between the least and largest backlash, sneaking up that distance. When the offset is the same at every speed: DirectionalCompensation (None, within the tolerance). Else DirectionalSneakUp at the fastest speed that agrees. An offset that goes the other way at the slowest speed (an overshoot) cannot be compensated, and it says so.
  6. The method tried: moves in to the mark from random places either side, and from 90 mm on each side, each measured against the mean of them all: how well moves agree with each other, whatever the machine slowly drifts by over the run.

What it found is in use at once, kept through Machine Setup (a step to undo), and shown on the tab with three graphs: the backlash at each sneak-up distance, the offset at each speed, and the errors once compensated.

docs.title: Periodic error
docs.text:
A belt pulley not quite round on its shaft, or a screw not quite straight, puts the head off where it is sent by a little, the same way on every turn: ahead for half a turn, behind for the other half, a wave along the axis as long as one turn. A gantry driven at both ends by two such pulleys also twists, the other axis off by a wave of its own. The camera cannot see it by itself, as it rides on the same axis, but the nozzle, some distance from the camera, lands where the axis puts it at that other place: parts land off by different amounts in different places on the board.

An X or Y axis's Periodic Error tab sets and measures it:

  • Drive Period: how far the axis travels for one turn of its drive: a belt pulley's teeth times the belt's pitch (15 teeth of HTD 3M: 45 mm), a screw's lead. 0: none.
  • Correction in Use: the wave in use, along the axis and across it (the other axis named), or none. jplacer's coordinates are where the head really is: each move is sent what puts the head there (a move along the axis moves the axis across it too), and the controller's report is read back the same way.
  • Scan Board measures it on the Job tab's chosen board, its fiducials checked first. The head camera goes to every footprint with nothing on its pads (a placement not yet placed, or a fiducial) and no more than 8 mm across, in order along the axis. There its pads are drawn where they should be (turned and mirrored as the camera is calibrated) and matched against the picture within 0.5 mm of there, as OpenPnP's template fiducial locator matches a footprint: shown on the camera's view, where they should be in its colour and where they were matched in green; a match scoring under 0.6 is not taken. Pads are copper from the same artwork as the fiducials, so they are a ruler with a mark every few millimetres.
