Package and the vision settings open their list on a click: a drop-down under the cell, as wide as its longest name, twelve at a time and scrolled for the rest, the one chosen now marked. Each change is saved at once.

Package opens the Packages tab's table instead, filtered and chosen from as a feeder's part is (see Choosing a part): a filter line where the cell was, Show and Columns to its right. Each word you type must start a word in the package's ID or description, and cap, res, ind, led and fid find packages by how their IDs start. It keeps its layout as a table of its own.

Sorting, choosing and copying rows, moving and widening columns, Columns, and the fields you can add to parts work as in every table: see Tables.

docs.title: The part's tabs
docs.text:
Under the table, the chosen part's tabs.

Library is what the library keeps of the part for matching it to boards' parts (see Choosing a part): its Value and Datasheet (a link or a file), the ID it is known by for good; its Identifiers, each an MPN or a Supplier PN with its Manufacturer / Supplier and Code (a board part with one of them is this part, without asking); and Also Known As, what boards' files call it: by Value and footprint (written value|footprint), Value or Footprint, each saying where it was learned and when (or typed). Names are learned when this part is chosen for a board's part with Remember ticked; the plus adds one, the cross deletes one. Manufacturers' Names… opens the manufacturers the library knows, a row each with its Name and its other names (commas between: Texas Instruments: TI, Texas Instruments Inc.), Add a Manufacturer and the cross to delete one; a BOM's manufacturer by any of them is that manufacturer. An MPN the library has under another manufacturer is offered but never taken unasked, and says so.

Packagings: how the part comes, a row each: Kind (Cut tape, Reel, Tray, Tube, Loose); for tape, its width (Tape [mm]: 8 to 56), the Pitch [mm] between pockets and whether it is Paper or Embossed; the part's Rotation [°] as it sits in the packaging (pin 1 against the tape's sprocket holes at 0), set once here; Quantity, how many a reel, tray or tube holds; a Note. Choosing another kind shows or hides the tape's columns. A feeder the part is loaded on takes its rotation, tape width and pitch from one of these (see The part's packaging).

Offers: where it is bought, a row each: Supplier, SKU (their part number), Packaging, MOQ (the least they sell), Price breaks (1: 0.0100, 100: 0.0050), Last price and Link.

Stock is what you have of the part: a lot is one reel, strip of cut tape, tray, tube or bag of it. Stock is what you have, not what is loaded on the machine. The page says how many are in stock and in how many lots, and lists each open lot: its Lot name, Packaging, how many it Holds, the feeder it is loaded On (see Feeders), Where kept, Date code and Note (the name, where kept, date code and note are changed here and kept at once). Receive Stock… adds a lot: its name on the shelf, packaging, Supplier and SKU (the part's first offer is filled in), Date code, Lot code, Where kept, Note, and how it came: Received (an order: its Quantity, the Cost of all of them and the Order) or Counted (found on the shelf). Receive is offered once the lot has a name and a quantity.

How many a lot holds is its ledger's: Ledger… lists every change to the lot in order, When, the Entry, the Quantity, what it Holds after, the Cost, the Reference and the Note, so a wrong figure shows where it went wrong. Below the list, add an entry: Used (taken for a job), Lost (dropped, mis-picked, thrown away), Counted (what it holds, counted now), Adjusted (more, 12, or fewer, -12, by hand) or Received (more came in), with its quantity, a reference and a note; Add to Ledger (or Return) keeps it at once. Close the Lot takes a lot used up or thrown away out of stock, its ledger kept (the Stock page counts the closed lots); Reopen the Lot puts it back.

Attrition is how many to allow for parts lost to mis-picks and drops, as a share of those placed; a job's shortages add it to what the job needs. Type the part's own Attrition [%], or leave it empty to use what the ledger measured: lost of all taken (used and lost), once any have been used. The page says what was measured.

Stock is kept in the library's file as each change is made, without saving.

Settings holds its Pick Conditions: Feed & Pick Retry Count, how many times the feed and pick is tried again for each placement (the nozzle is cleared, and the part discarded, after each failed try).

Bottom Vision Settings and Fiducial Vision Settings show the vision settings the part uses (its own, else its package's, else the machine's), as on the Vision tab: a change is a change to those settings, for everything that uses them. While the part uses settings it shares, Specialize for the part makes a copy of them, named after the part, for this part alone. Once it has its own, Use Package package's Settings (or Use the Machine's Default Settings, its package having none) puts it back on those, after asking; its own stay on the Vision tab, used by nothing.

docs.title: Undo and Redo
docs.text: Every change to the library is a step Edit ▸ Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes back and Edit ▸ Redo (Ctrl+Y) makes again: a part or package made, changed or deleted (several deleted at once are one step), a field changed on a part's or package's pages, a footprint added, changed or deleted, the manufacturers' names, and what choosing a part for a board taught the library (a name remembered, a part added). Each says what it would undo or redo: "Undo Delete Part R0603-10k", "Undo Change Package SOT-23", "Undo Delete 3 Parts", "Undo New Footprint SOT-23-3". A part or package put back by Undo is the same one, its place in the list kept. Undo and Redo go through the library's changes, Machine Setup's and the other tables' together, the last made first. The last 200 steps are kept. Stock (lots and their ledger) is kept as it is made and is not undone.

docs.title: Pipeline Editor
docs.text:
Some of OpenPnP's vision is done by a pipeline: a list of stages that each do one thing to the camera's picture (blur it, threshold it, find circles in it, draw what was found) and hand the result to the next. jplacer runs OpenPnP's pipelines stage for stage and writes them back as OpenPnP does, so a pipeline brought over from OpenPnP runs here, and one tuned here runs in OpenPnP. Every stage OpenPnP's editor offers can be added and run.

Everything jplacer finds with a camera is found by a pipeline, as OpenPnP finds it: fiducials, the homing mark, strip feeders' holes, parts in bottom vision, nozzle tips and calibration marks.

docs.title: Opening it
docs.text:
A strip feeder's page has Edit Pipeline... and Reset Pipeline under Vision. Edit Pipeline... opens the editor on the feeder's pipeline (OpenPnP's default strip feeder pipeline when the feeder has none), with the head camera's picture. Reset Pipeline puts the default pipeline back.

Bottom vision and fiducial settings have it too, under Pipeline ▸ Edit... on their pages (the Vision tab, a part's or a package's): see Vision.

The editor opens in a window of its own, nine tenths of the main window's size. The pipeline is run once as it opens, and again after every change, so the result of each stage is always the current one. Its camera runs, as every camera does while the machine is on, its picture on screen or not.

docs.title: The picture it is given
docs.text: As in OpenPnP, a pipeline is given the camera's picture corrected, once the camera is calibrated: the lens's bending taken out and the machine square to the picture, at one scale both ways, centred on the point the camera looks at, as the camera's straightened view shows it (its Crop All Invalid Pixels the same). Edges straight on the board are straight in it, and what the camera does not see is black. What a pipeline finds is placed on the machine through that corrected picture. This is so wherever a pipeline runs: in a job (fiducials, bottom vision, feeders), in a test, from a script and in this editor. A camera not yet calibrated gives its picture as taken. A camera's own calibration pipeline is the exception: it measures the lens, so it is given the picture as taken.

docs.title: The stages
docs.text:
The left side lists the stages in the order they run: Enabled (an unticked stage is skipped), Name (double-click to rename; other stages refer to it by this name) and Stage, its kind. Drag a stage up or down to run it at another place. Below the list, the chosen stage's description; below that, its settings, each with its own description as its tooltip. A setting the feeder or vision operation sets each time the pipeline runs is shown, not edited, with "Controlled by pipeline caller" and the value it was given.

Tool Update picture from current view Runs the pipeline again on a new picture from the camera. New stage... Adds a stage of the kind chosen at the end, named so no other stage has its name. Delete Stage Removes the chosen stage. Copy pipeline to clipboard The whole pipeline as OpenPnP's text, for pasting into OpenPnP or another feeder. Create pipeline from clipboard Replaces the stages with a pipeline copied from OpenPnP or jplacer.

docs.title: The results
docs.text:
The right side shows a stage's result: its name, how long it took and how long the whole pipeline took; its picture; and, below, what it found (circles, rectangles, key points…), one to a line. The arrows show the first, previous, next and last stage. Pin keeps showing the pinned stage's result while you choose others and change their settings. The colour button switches between true colours (a picture in HSV or HLS shown as it looks) and the picture's numbers shown as if they were blue, green, red.

Over the picture, the line under it gives the colour of the pixel under the mouse (as RGB and as full-range HSV, the numbers a mask stage wants) and its place in pixels; over something found, what was found there. For an AffineWarp stage it also gives the place in the stage's length units from the camera's centre.

When the pipeline stops (no picture from its camera, say), the text below the picture begins with why; nothing else interrupts you, so holding a setting's arrow keeps changing it.

docs.title: Closing it
docs.text: Closed after a change, the editor asks Save pipeline changes?: Yes keeps them, No puts the pipeline back as it was, Cancel goes back to editing with the changes still there.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text: Edit ▸ Preferences… opens the settings, on three tabs: General, Keys and Jog. Each one takes effect and is saved the moment you change it (a text box when you press Return or Tab, or leave it; Escape puts back what it had), so there is no Apply button: close the window with Close when you are done. The window can be made bigger by dragging its edge.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text: Theme Dark (as jplacer is first installed), Light, or As the desktop is set: dark or light as the desktop's own setting is when jplacer opens or the theme is chosen (GNOME's colour scheme, or Windows' app mode); dark when the desktop does not say. Interface scale How big the whole interface is: its controls and the text in them grow together, and the panels make room, so nothing is magnified or blurred. As the screen asks (as first installed) follows the screen's pixel density; or choose 100 % to 200 %.

docs.title: General
docs.text: Tear-off menus (drag a menu off into its own window) When ticked, a menu can be dragged off the menu bar into a small window of its own that stays open, which is handy for a menu you use often. Off when jplacer is first installed. The change applies the next time you open a menu. Show jplacer in the applications menu When ticked, jplacer keeps an entry for itself in your desktop's applications menu (see Getting started). Unticking it removes the entry and its icon. On when jplacer is first installed. This row only appears when jplacer is running as an AppImage.

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text: Check the job before each run When ticked, Start first lists what the job's check found (things to put right, check or note), with Start Anyway (see Checking the job). Unticked, Start runs the job at once; something that would stop the run is still listed, as the run cannot start. Job ▸ Check Job… lists everything at any time. On when jplacer is first installed.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: Backups kept Each time jplacer starts, before it changes anything, it copies its settings (jplacer.json) and every machine (the cells folder) into backups/<date and time>/ beside them, a rolling set: past this many, the oldest copy is let go. 20 when jplacer is first installed; 0 takes none. The log says where each copy went. To go back to one, copy its files over those beside the backups folder while jplacer is closed.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text: Save vision pictures for debugging What OpenPnP does at its Debug log level. While ticked, every vision pipeline run (bottom vision, fiducials, feeders, a camera's or a nozzle tip's calibration) keeps each of its stages' pictures in a folder of its own, log/vision/<date and time>_<what it was for>/ beside jplacer's settings, numbered in the stages' order (01_<stage>.png, 02_<stage>.png…), with stages.txt saying each stage's class, how long it took and what it found. A pipeline's ImageWriteDebug stages write too, into org.openpnp.vision.pipeline.stages.ImageWriteDebug/ there, as OpenPnP's do. Off when jplacer is first installed; ticking and unticking take effect at once. Keep at most (MB) How much vision debugging keeps, its runs' folders and ImageWriteDebug's pictures together: past it, the oldest are deleted first as new ones come, the newest always kept; lowered, it trims at once. 1000 MB to begin with; 0 keeps everything, as OpenPnP does (a day of it filled 11 GB).

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
Check for updates when jplacer opens When ticked, jplacer looks for a newer version each time it starts, and tells you only if it finds one. On when jplacer is first installed. Include beta versions When ticked, you are offered beta versions as well as full releases. Beta versions get new features first and have had less testing. Off when jplacer is first installed. Check Now Closes Preferences and looks for a newer version straight away, as Help ▸ Check For Updates… does.

More about how updates work is in Updates and betas.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Every function that can be given a key is listed, by menu: File, Edit, Machine, Jog (the Jog panel's buttons), Help, the Jog panel's steps (Jog Distance, Jog Speed; see Jog below), and Tables (Show View 1 to 9, Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9: the table last clicked in shows that view; see Views). Each has a box showing its key, or None.

  • Click a function's box, and it reads "Press a key...": press the key, with Ctrl, Alt or Shift if you want them. Escape leaves the key as it was. A plain key (an arrow, a digit, a letter) can be given, as well as one with Ctrl, Alt or Shift; Tab cannot, as it moves between fields.
  • A key belongs to one function. Given to another, it is taken from the one that had it, and the line under the list says so.
  • Clear takes a function's key off. Reset All puts every function's own key back.

The keys start as OpenPnP's: Ctrl+Right / Left / Up / Down for X and Y, Ctrl+' and Ctrl+/ for Z, Ctrl+, and Ctrl+. to turn, Ctrl+= and Ctrl+- for the distance, Ctrl+Shift+P to park, and so on, with Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y for Undo and Redo, Ctrl+H to home, and Escape to stop. Emergency Stop has no key until you give it one, so a slip of the finger cannot reset the controllers.

A key goes to the box you are typing in first: a digit or an arrow given to a jog function still types or moves the cursor there, and does its function only where nothing else uses it. A menu shows each entry's key, and the Jog panel's buttons say theirs when you hover over them.

docs.title: Jog
docs.text:
The Jog panel's steps, numbers apart, smallest first:

Distance steps (mm or degrees) What the distance slider steps through, and Raise / Lower Jog Increment go to (and the First to Fifth Jog Increment pick from). 0.001 to 1000. It starts as 0.01 0.1 1 10 25 50 100. Speed steps (%) Marked on the speed slider; Faster and Slower go to the next one up or down from the speed now. 1 to 100. It starts as 10 25 50 75 100.

Each step is also listed on the Keys tab (Distance 1, Speed 25%) to be given a key: the digit 1 for 1 mm and 2 for 10 mm, say. Steps that make no sense (a word, a step smaller than the one before) are not taken, and the tab says why. Emptied, a box goes back to the steps jplacer starts with.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text: Every table in jplacer works the same way: the parts, packages and their pads, boards, panels and their placements, the job's boards, feeders and vision settings. You can sort it, choose rows, move, widen and hide its columns, and add fields of your own to what its rows are.

docs.title: Sorting, choosing and copying
docs.text: Click a column's heading to sort by it; click it again to turn it round. Clicking another heading sorts by that first and by the earlier ones after it (up to three); the later ones' arrows are fainter. Choose several rows with Shift+click and Ctrl+click; Ctrl+A chooses them all, and Ctrl+C copies the chosen rows, a tab between cells (in the columns' order as shown).

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Search, at the right of a toolbar, shows only the rows with the text typed anywhere in them, in any column, a hidden one's too, whatever its case. The text is a regular expression: ^C0402 finds rows with something starting C0402. Beside it, while it searches, how many rows it leaves of how many (12 of 340), and in each cell what it matched is marked. A row found only in a column the table does not show has a mark at its start, and pointing at it says which column it was found in. The ✕ at its right end empties it.

A column's heading and a colon first searches that column alone: lcsc: C15 finds the rows whose LCSC starts with or holds C15, and lcsc: alone the rows with anything in it. As you type the start of a column's heading, the rest of it shows greyed after what you typed; Tab (or → at the end) takes it, with the colon. A colon after something that is no column's heading (http://) is part of the search.

docs.title: Moving and widening columns
docs.text: Drag a heading's edge to widen a column; the columns after it give way. Drag a heading sideways to move its column. While it is dragged the table shows how it will look: the column floats with the pointer and the others move aside to make its place. Letting go keeps it there; Escape puts every column back as it was. Each table keeps its columns' order, widths and sort as you leave them, the next time jplacer starts too. They are kept by what each column is, not by its heading, so a column you rename keeps its place.

docs.title: Views
docs.text:
A view is a table's layout kept under a name: which columns it shows, their order and widths, and its sort. Each table has its own, and switching between them changes the whole layout in one click: a simple view, a supplier's, a production view, your own. Each starts with two: Standard, the table as jplacer ships it, and All Fields, every column, always (those you add later too; its ticks in Columns are greyed, as it hides none). Whatever you change in a view (a column shown or hidden, moved, widened, a sort) is kept in that view as you change it: there is nothing to save.

Beside Columns on the toolbar, each view has a button showing its icon, its name in its tooltip; the view shown is lit. Click one to show it, or press Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 in the table for its first nine (the keys can be changed in Edit ▸ Preferences…, as Show View 1 to 9). Drag a button along the row to move its view there. Right-click it for its own menu:

Entry Show "name" Shows it. Rename… Gives it another name. Icon The icon its button shows: List, Columns, Star, Truck, Wrench, Eye, Person, Clipboard, Tag, Flag, Box, Gear or Check. Duplicate A copy of it beside it (as shown now, changes and all), shown. Locked Keeps the view as it is: a change while it is shown lasts only until another view is shown, its button marked with a dot meanwhile. Unlocked while changed, the change is its own. Keeps Its Search The view keeps the search typed while it is shown, and puts it back in Search whenever it is shown again: a production view of feeders showing only those enabled, a view of the parts with no height. Revert View (the view shown) Puts it back as it was kept, the changes since it was shown undone. Delete View Takes it away (a table keeps one view at least).

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Columns (the table icon), at the end of a toolbar's icons after a divider, starts with the table's views: each one (the one shown ticked, (changed) after a locked one changed), New View… (a view made from the one shown, named as you say, with an icon no other view has yet) and This View, the view shown's own menu. Then it chooses which columns the table shows: a tick for each column shown; click one to hide it or to show it again in its place, at the width it had. The last column showing cannot be hidden. Reset Columns at the bottom shows them all again, as they first were. Which columns are shown is kept with the rest of the table's layout, each table its own. The tables on the Job, Boards, Panels, Parts, Packages, Vision, Feeders and Issues & Solutions tabs have it and their views, the footprint's pads too, and the table a feeder's Part or a part's Package drops has them beside its filter (its views its own, though no fields are added or edited from it, as it is only chosen from). A table with no view buttons (those in a window of their own) is a plain table: its Columns and its headings' menu show and hide its columns, and offer no views and no fields to add or edit.

Right-click a heading for that column's menu: Hide "name", Show in Every View (shown in each of the table's views, not only the one shown), Add Field After "name"…, Edit Field "name"… and Reset Columns.

docs.title: Editing many rows, pasting and undo
docs.text:
A value typed into a cell, a tick or a choice, in a row that is one of several chosen, goes into every row chosen: choose 50 parts, type LCSC in one row's Supplier, and it is in all 50. Choose the rows, then type (or press F2) in the cell, tick it, or pick its choice; a double-click in one of the chosen rows edits them all too, where a plain click on one chooses it alone. A row that cannot take the value (one whose cell cannot be changed) is left as it is; a value refused by one row is taken by none, the cell staying open to put it right. The status line says how many were changed.

Ctrl+V pastes what Ctrl+C copied, or a block of cells copied from a spreadsheet (a tab between cells, a line a row): from the chosen cell, down the rows and along the columns as the table shows them. One value goes into every row chosen. A cell that cannot be changed is passed over, and the status line says how many. A value a cell cannot take (a word for a number, a choice it does not have) and nothing at all is pasted, the first few refused named.

Each change is one step Edit ▸ Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes back and Edit ▸ Redo (Ctrl+Y) makes again, however many cells it changed, named for it ("Undo Change Rank of 12 Placements", "Undo Change 3 Cells of 2 Rows"). The library's tables (parts, packages and their pads) are undone as the library's changes are (see Parts); the others' steps are kept with Machine Setup's and the library's, the last made first, the last 200 of them.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Each column of a table of things (parts, placements, feeders…) is one of their fields. jplacer has its own, the columns each table has always had, and you can add as many of your own as you want: an LCSC part number, a supplier, a reel's size, a customer's order number. A field belongs to the kind of thing, not to one table: a field added to placements is a column of the Job tab's placements, a panel's fiducials, and every other table of placements. And the import offers each one to fill (see Importing a board).

Add Field…, in Columns and on a heading's menu, adds one. Give it a Name (unique among that kind's fields, and without a colon), a Type, and the Import matches: the headings of a CAD file's or BOM's column that the import takes for it, commas between (its name always counts, and upper and lower case, spaces and punctuation do not matter). It shows in the table you added it from, at the end or after the column whose heading you right-clicked, and is hidden in the other tables of its kind until you tick it in their Columns.

The type says how its values are typed and shown:

Type Typed as Shown Text anything as typed Number a number (12, -0.5, 12,5) as typed, on the right, sorted as numbers Length a length in any units (1.2, 40mil, 0.5in); without units, the System Units in the System Units, sorted by length Yes/No a tick box Choice one of its Choices (commas between when you make it) picked from its list; the empty one at the end takes it out

A value that is not one of its type is refused, and the cell stays open to put it right. Emptying a cell takes its value out.

Edit Fields… (in Columns) lists every field of that kind: its name, its type (jplacer's own for its fields), whose it is, whether jplacer needs it, its import matches, and how many have a value in each of yours. Edit…, or a double-click, or Edit Field "name"… on a heading, opens the field: rename any field, and change the import matches of one an import fills; a field of yours also its type and choices. Changing a field of yours to another type reads its values again as that type. Those it cannot read are named first, and emptied once you agree.

Delete… takes a field of yours away with its values (how many have one is said first). A field of jplacer's you have no use for is Removed…: it leaves every table, the import and the search, its values staying as they are (jplacer uses some of them itself), until Restore in Edit Fields… brings it back. The fields jplacer cannot work without have no Delete…:

Table of Kept always Parts ID, Height, Package Packages ID Pads Name, X, Y, Width, Length, Rot. Placements ID, Part, Side, X, Y, Rot. Boards and panels where they lie Board/Panel Id, Side, X, Y, Z, Rot., Enabled? Boards, Panels Board Name, Panel Name Feeders ID, Name, Part, Type, Enabled Vision settings Name

The fields are kept in fields.json in the configuration folder. Each thing keeps its own values with it: a part's, a package's and its pads' in the library, a placement's and a board's in the board's file, a panel's in its file, the job's boards and the job's own in the job, a feeder's in feeders.json, vision settings' in vision-settings.json. A placement's values are its board's: on the Job tab, a board used more than once keeps no values of its own, so there they are shown and not changed.

docs.title: Job fields
docs.text: A job has no table of its own, so its fields are in Job ▸ Job Fields…: a row for each field added to jobs, its value changed in place, and Add Field… and Edit Fields… as every table has them. The job's values are kept in its file.

docs.title: Updates and betas
docs.text: jplacer updates itself. Updates come from the project's GitHub releases.

docs.title: When it looks
docs.text:
• When jplacer opens, unless you have turned that off in Preferences. It only speaks up when there is a newer version: no internet connection, for example, is not worth interrupting you for every time.
  • Help ▸ Check For Updates… (or Check Now in Preferences). Because you asked, you are told every answer: a newer version, that you are up to date, or that it could not check and why.

docs.title: Installing an update
docs.text:
When there is a newer version, jplacer says which version is available and which you have, and asks whether to download and install it.

  • Update downloads it, with a progress window you can cancel. When the download is complete, jplacer closes, puts the new version in place and starts it again.
  • Not now leaves it for later. Tick Don't ask about version again first and that version is not offered when jplacer opens; a later version is, and Check For Updates… still finds it.

Every download is checked against the checksum published with the release before anything is changed. A download that does not match is not installed, and nothing is changed if a download fails.

On Linux the AppImage updates itself: the new one replaces it. On Windows the update is the new version's installer, run once jplacer has closed without asking anything (you see its progress), which installs over the old one and starts the new. A copy of jplacer built from source, or unzipped from the Windows zip, tells you an update is available but cannot install it.

docs.title: Beta versions
docs.text: Beta versions are released before a full release so new features can be tried early. They are offered only if you tick Include beta versions in Preferences. A beta is numbered below the release it leads to (0.1.2-beta.1 comes before 0.1.2), so when that release comes out it is offered to you as usual.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text: The Vision tab (in the work area, after Packages, as in OpenPnP) lists the vision settings parts, packages and the machine use: Bottom Vision Settings (how a part on the nozzle is looked at from below) and Fiducial Vision Settings (how a fiducial is found). They are kept in vision-settings.json in jplacer's configuration folder, each as OpenPnP keeps it, pipeline and all. Until there is one, OpenPnP's vision-settings.xml is read: one copied into the folder, else OpenPnP's defaults; the next save writes vision-settings.json, and the .xml is not read again.

docs.title: The toolbar and table
docs.text:
Button New Settings (plus) Makes new settings of the type shown, named after their kind, and chooses them. Delete Settings (cross) Deletes the chosen settings, after asking. Settings in use are not deleted: it says what uses them. Copy Vision Settings to Clipboard Puts the chosen settings on the clipboard as text. Create Vision Settings from Clipboard Makes settings from what the clipboard holds, each with a new id; a name already used gets " (Copy)".

Type, at the right, chooses which are shown: BottomVision or FiducialVision.

The table has Name (changed in place, except the stock settings', whose id says "Stock") and Assigned To: what uses them. That is the stock settings themselves, Bottom Vision or Fiducal Locator for the machine's default (as OpenPnP spells it), then the packages, then the parts, by ID.

As OpenPnP does each time it starts, jplacer keeps OpenPnP's stock settings there with OpenPnP's stock pipelines: bottom vision's - Stock Bottom Vision Settings -, - Rectlinear Symmetry Bottom Vision Settings - and - Whole Part Body Bottom Vision Settings -, and the fiducials' - Stock Fiducial Vision Settings - and - Footprint Fiducial Vision Settings -; with none yet, the machine's defaults, - Default Machine Bottom Vision - and - Default Machine Fiducial Locator -, start as the stock ones.

docs.title: The settings
docs.text:
Under the table, the chosen settings' page. General: Name, Assigned to, Enabled?, and Reset to Default, which gives them the values of the machine's default settings of their kind (the machine's default itself the stock settings' values), keeping their name, after asking. Specializing and generalizing are done from a part's or package's page (see Parts and Packages).

Bottom Vision Settings add Pre-rotate (Default, AlwaysOn, AlwaysOff), Rotation (Adjust, Full), Part size check (Disabled, BodySize, PadExtents) with its Size tolerance (%), and Vision Offsets: Asymmetric? (the contacts are off the part's centre by design) and the Vision Center Offsets. A job uses them all, as OpenPnP's bottom vision does: Enabled?, Pre-rotate (Default: as the machine's bottom vision says), Rotation (Adjust: the part taken as turned less than 45° either way; Full: all the way round), the Part size check (the part as measured, its width and length, within the Size tolerance of its body, or of its pads' extent; else the alignment fails, saying which, the nominal, the limit and what was measured: "Part R1 width too small: nominal 3.000mm, limit 2.400mm, measured 1.277mm"), and the Vision Center Offsets, taken off what is found, turned as the part is (see Running the job). A part seen whole is looked for only where it can be: within how far its pads and body reach from its middle, plus its nozzle tip's Max Pick Tolerance (the pipeline's part mask), not the whole of the tip's Max Part Diameter, so whatever else is bright round the tip is not taken for it.

Test Alignment aligns the part on the nozzle chosen on the Jog panel over the camera looking up, as a job would at the Placement Angle (the machine's test alignment angle), and shows what it found on the camera ("R1 | X:0.012 Y:-0.034 C:0.512 Δ:0.036"); with Center After Test it then moves the part over the camera's centre, turned to the angle, at the height it was seen at (in focus, its footprint's reticle over it), moving straight there without lifting the part, and shows a fresh picture of it once the camera has settled, as OpenPnP's. With the nozzle's Align with Part? (its aligning rotation mode), the part's turn on the nozzle is taken into the nozzle's rotation, as a job's alignment does: the nozzle then reads the part's angle (the DRO, and the reticle drawn over the part at it). On a paused run, with the run's part on that nozzle already aligned, what Test Alignment finds is what the run then places it with, in place of its own alignment ("Test Alignment taken for R1"). The nozzle must hold a part (picked with Pick on the Feeders or Parts tab, or by a job), of the part or package the page is for, whose bottom vision these settings are; else it says what is wrong ("Nozzle N1 does not have a part loaded"). Detect Offsets is for an asymmetric part: centre it over the camera by hand first; it aligns and centres the part at 0°, and adds the difference to the Vision Center Offsets.

Fiducial Vision Settings add the Fiducial Locator: Max. Vision Passes, Max. Linear Offset, Parallax Diameter and Parallax Angle. A fiducial check uses them (see Jobs): the fiducial is looked at again, centred, up to the passes, until a look moves it less than the max linear offset; with a parallax diameter, it is looked at from either side of it, that far apart and turned by the angle, and the middle taken. The fiducial is found by the settings' pipeline, as OpenPnP finds it, no farther from where it should be than their Max. Distance (their pipeline's parameter; for a pipeline without one, the machine's Fiducial Locator's). Settings not enabled stop the check. Test Fiducial Locator finds the fiducial nearest where the head camera is (the part's or package's footprint; on the Vision tab, a round 1 mm fiducial) as a fiducial check would, and moves the camera onto it.

A part uses its own settings, else its package's, else the machine's (OpenPnP's part alignment and fiducial locator, brought in with an OpenPnP machine).

docs.title: The pipeline
docs.text:
Both kinds keep OpenPnP's vision pipeline with them (OpenPnP's stock pipeline for the kind until they have one of their own). The Pipeline row works it as OpenPnP's does: Edit... opens it in the Pipeline Editor; Reset puts back the machine's default settings' pipeline (or, for the machine's default settings themselves, the stock one), after asking; the copy button puts the pipeline on the clipboard as OpenPnP's text, and the paste button replaces it with one from the clipboard, after asking.

Under it, a slider for each of the pipeline's parameters (its ParameterNumeric and ParameterBool stages: a threshold, a least detail size, a search distance), named and explained as the pipeline names them. The value is kept with these settings, not in the pipeline, so settings that share a pipeline can each tune it. Moving a slider runs the pipeline on the camera and shows the stage the parameter affects, then the result, on the camera's view for three seconds each, with the parameter's name and value over them ("Threshold = 204").

The pipeline is run as OpenPnP prepares it: a fiducial's on the head camera, with its package's footprint (on the Vision tab, a round 1 mm fiducial); bottom vision's on the camera looking up, with the package of the part or package the page is for (on the Vision tab, the part chosen on the Parts tab, else the package chosen on the Packages tab) turned by the machine's test alignment angle, over the camera's centre.

• Choosing another part for a feeder resets its feed count, as Reset does, so the new tape is fed from its first part.
  • A strip feeder's Auto Setup puts the camera over the first part, and the next pick goes there, even after the feeder has fed parts with vision: the holes vision had found were kept and the pick worked out from them until Reset was pressed. Typing or capturing a hole location forgets them too.
  • A part discarded by hand while a job is paused (after bottom vision could not find it, say) is picked again when the job goes on: before, the job went back to look for it on the empty nozzle.
  • A job wastes less time between a place and the next pick. The job's state was told to the signalers before every step, each time waiting for the screen to draw its next frame (up to 160 ms right after a place), and each step's look at the job waited for a frame too: on the bench 1.4 s went by at safe Z between placements.
  • Backlash Off Below Safe Z now only affects jogs made while a nozzle is down. Before, it switched the machine's compensation off whenever a nozzle went below safe Z and back on a moment after it came up, too late for the next move: a job's move to the place after bottom vision, bottom vision's own correcting move, and Position Nozzle after Test Alignment all went without backlash compensation.
  • An X or Y axis's drive that puts the head off the same way every turn (a belt pulley not quite round on its shaft) can be measured and corrected: Machine Setup › the axis › Periodic Error. Set the Drive Period (a pulley's teeth times the belt's pitch), then Scan Board finds every bare footprint's pads on the Job tab's chosen board with the camera and fits the wave from them; Apply puts it in use for every move.
  • A tip put on for a pick on the Feeders tab (Change On Manual Pick) is now measured straight after, as its Auto Recalibration says. Before, only a job measured it, and a manual pick went ahead with its runout unknown.
  • Jog's Position Nozzle comes the last of the way down at the tip's Approach Speed, as a pick or place does. Before, it went straight down at full speed.
  • The log says whenever backlash compensation is turned off or on, and why.
  • Jog's Position Nozzle with a part aligned on it (Test Alignment) puts the part's centre where the camera looks, not the nozzle's, as a job's place does. Before, the part landed off by its offset on the nozzle (0.4 mm on the bench), on the board and back over the bottom camera alike.
  • After Jog's Position Nozzle, Position Camera brings the camera back exactly where it was: over the part's centre, whether the part is still held or has been put down, and with the nozzle's lean taken at the height the nozzle went down to. Before, it went over the nozzle's centre instead (0.31 mm off the place on the bench), and after Park Z with the camera chosen it took the lean at safe height (nearly 1 mm off).
  • Position Nozzle says, under the jog buttons, when the camera's Z is at safe height and so the nozzle stays up (Park Z with the camera chosen puts it there). On the bench a part was let go of 24 mm up, taken to be on the board.
  • Every change made in Machine Setup is put in use and saved at once, as OpenPnP's Apply does. Before, one problem anywhere (an axis's controller set to none, say) held every later change back without a word but a line under the settings: a test object thickness and a backlash offset typed in were neither used nor saved for half an hour. A problem is now said in a dialog, listed, and refused where it is used: Home says in a dialog that an axis has no controller, and a cell file with one loads (it would not open before). Changes made while a calibration runs wait until it ends (a change mid-way through a backlash calibration had thrown it off: "axis x would go to 8515…").
  • Backlash Calibrate measures and chooses as OpenPnP's calibration does: speed control and a step test first, the backlash wound from 90 mm and coming in from distances, the offset found at each speed by compensated moves, and OpenPnP's rules for the method. A one-sided offset is the backlash measured after a long move, not how far the play takes to level off (which came to 1.5 and 2 mm on the bench, an overshoot that would hit a tip changer's slots), nor the short-reversal play (0.018 mm on the bench's Y, too little for a long move). Calibrate the X and Y axes again. A calibration that stops says why in a dialog.
  • Backlash Off Below Safe Z no longer turns backlash compensation off with the head at safe Z: safe Z is judged by where the Z was sent, as OpenPnP does. A Z axis stops on its nearest step, a few thousandths below safe Z, which counted as below it, so with the option ticked the compensation was off for nearly every move, picks and places included, and a nozzle landed differently depending on the side it came from.
  • Part detection's Ratio method, for a vacuum sensor on the pump's side of the valve: each level taken as a share of the pump's just before, so a pump cycling on and off does not count. Measure sets it where the sensor reads the pump.
  • Jog's Position Camera goes over where the nozzle's tip really is: its runout at its angle, and its lean at the camera's height. Before, Position Nozzle and Position Camera there and back walked the head by the runout each time (a part over the bottom camera crept to its corner), and the camera sent to a nozzle up at safe Z after a place landed about 1 mm beside the part. The position readout and places captured from a nozzle take its runout in too.
  • Jogging a nozzle with a lean up or down keeps its tip over the same place, as turning it already did against its runout.
  • A nozzle tip can be Z-calibrated at the head's primary fiducial (Tool Changer tab, Touch At: Primary Fiducial) instead of a touch location of its own: one place for every tip, which moves with the calibration rig.
  • A nozzle tip's part detection ranges can be measured instead of guessed (Part Detection tab: Part Off's Measure, Part On's Without Part and With Part, each switching the vacuum off again after): the machine reads its own vacuum, as each check does, and sets each range from where a part and no part (an open and a blocked nozzle, for Part Off) are told apart, wide enough for the pump's level to drift. Where the sensor reads the pump's side of the valve, Part Off reads as the valve closes (Valve close 0). A method that cannot tell the two apart gives way to the one that can; when neither can, it says so and sets nothing.

• What fails with nothing waiting on it is said in a dialog, with why: a nozzle tip's Calibrate now, the Jog panel's Pick and Place, Detect Firmware, a controller's unasked error, a lost connection. Before, these were said to no one: Calibrate now went down to the touch location and stopped there without a word (a tip probing by vacuum needs a Part Off sensing method).
  • The calibration test object is given by its thickness (Test Object Thickness, with Capture: the nozzle tip touching it) and lies on the primary fiducial; a test object Z kept before is read as its thickness. The precise offsets calibration looks for it there. Before, it looked wherever the feature was last sized or the camera happened to be.
  • Nozzle offsets can be calibrated at two heights (Two Heights?, on the head's Calibration Rig and a nozzle's Calibration tab): the nozzle carries the test object from the primary fiducial to the secondary, calibrates there too and carries it back, which gives how far its tip moves in X and Y as it goes up and down (its lean). Every move of the nozzle then takes that into account, so a part lands where it is sent at board height as well as at the height calibrated at. The Calibration tab shows the lean and each height's angles.
  • Issues & Solutions' precise nozzle offsets calibration takes the test object's size in mm (Test Object Diameter), the same value as the nozzle's Calibration tab. Before, it was a Feature diameter in pixels.
  • The precise nozzle offsets calibration uses the test object's size as set or detected. Before, it measured the object again where the camera happened to be, overwrote the size, and failed when it was not found there.
  • After homing, the bottom camera's light stays on while the tip's runout is measured. Before, it could be switched off as the measuring began, so the runout pictures were taken in the dark.
  • Moving a nozzle to the head's Primary Fiducial (or another of the head's places) no longer turns it to the fiducial's diameter in degrees, and capturing with the nozzle no longer writes its angle into the Diameter.
  • Changing a head's settings (the test object's size or place, the calibration rig, park) no longer restarts the cameras. Before, the cameras flashed "Starting…", and a precise calibration straight after Detect then failed to find the test object, because the restarted camera had lost the exposure Detect had just tuned.
  • Preferences > Jobs > Check the job before each run: unticked, Start runs the job at once instead of first listing what the job's check found. Anything that would stop the run is still shown. On by default.
  • A nozzle's Calibration tab has Check Placement: the test object picked off the primary fiducial and put back as a job places a part (aligned on the bottom camera at four angles, put back with the job's correction), the head camera measuring where it landed. It says how far off it lands, and splits that into the drift at pick and let-go, bottom vision's bias, and the nozzle's offset error at the place height, so where an error comes from can be seen.
  • A nozzle's lean (from a calibration at two heights) is shown with its offsets on its Configuration tab and can be changed there, or set to 0 for none.
  • Jog's Position Nozzle takes the nozzle down to the camera's height (the board's or a feeder's), its tip on the point the camera looks at, as a feeder's Position Nozzle goes to the pick; with a part on the nozzle, the part's bottom goes to that height. Before, it stopped at safe Z, and lowering it by hand could land off where the nozzle leans.
  • A tip's calibration, the precise offsets calibration and Check Placement no longer refuse when jplacer takes a part to be on the nozzle (one let go by hand still counts): the part is discarded first, then they go on. A tip change forgets the part, so the new tip's automatic calibration is no longer refused (before, it was refused with only a passing status line). Check Placement calibrates the tip's runout first when it has none on that nozzle.
  • Check Placement tells apart and takes out the test object's own offset (a dot whose centre on top is not its centre underneath turned every placement 0.2 to 0.3 mm off on bench), keeps every picture it takes with what it looked for and found drawn on it, and shows the found circle on the camera.
  • A nozzle tip can come the last of the way down to a pick or place slowly, and lift slowly after it (Approach Height, Approach Speed, Lift Speed on its Configuration tab; off until an Approach Height is given). On bench a fast lift after letting go disturbed the part.
  • Measurements (Check Placement's result, a camera's settling trace and tuned values, a tip's last vacuum readings, a controller's detected firmware) are saved to the machine's file as they are made. Before, they waited for the next settings change, and a tip change could save over them.

• A nozzle's Offset Wizard tab in Machine Setup is now its Calibration tab. It runs the precise offsets calibration with the test object (the one Issues & Solutions offers) as well as the rough one by a mark. It keeps the nozzle's last 10 calibrations: when and how each ran, the offsets before and the ones found, and the change. A graph shows each angle's estimate around the correction, so an outlier (a bad find, or the test object slipping) stands out; a second graph shows how closely precise runs repeat.
  • The runout graph on a nozzle tip's Calibration tab names its circle "runout"; before, it was mislabelled "outlier limit".

• A nozzle's Kind (ReferenceNozzle or ContactProbeNozzle) can be changed in Machine Setup, keeping its settings, so an existing nozzle can find part and feeder heights by vacuum sensing or a contact sensor. Before, only a new nozzle could be a ContactProbeNozzle.
  • Quitting while a job runs or is paused stops the job (nozzles emptied, head parked) and quits, instead of saying to stop it first.
  • Stop pressed while a step that then fails is under way still empties the nozzles and parks the head. Before, the run just stopped where it was.
  • A run paused when the machine's connection was lost can be stopped (Stop was greyed, and jplacer would not quit while the run was paused).
  • A placement deleted while a job runs or is paused, or a board taken out of the job, is left out of the run: its part, if already picked, is discarded. Before, the run went on with it and took the part to the board's origin (past the machine's limits on one machine, which stopped the run). Removing a board mid-run could also crash.
  • Board Nudge's Apply moves the board by what was jogged, in X and Y: it moved nothing (the board let go of as the instructions closed, before it was moved).
  • Test Alignment on a nozzle with Align with Part? takes the part's turn into the nozzle's rotation, as a run and OpenPnP do: the bottom camera's reticle then lies over the part, not turned by how far the part sat turned on the nozzle.
  • Bottom vision refuses a part its looks turned further in all than a look can tell (45 degrees; 180 with Rotation Full), instead of placing it turned: a square part on a tip as wide as it was seen round and placed 90 degrees out. Each look is now in the log, with how far off and turned it saw the part.
  • A nozzle turned past 180 degrees (taken the short way, then brought back into range) no longer turns the long way round on its next move: a bottom vision pass correcting a part by a degree turned it 361 degrees, slowly.
  • Bottom vision's looks after the first (Max. vision passes, when a part is further off than Max. linear or angular offset) move straight across at the camera's height, as OpenPnP's, not up to Safe Z and back down.
  • Bottom vision takes the nozzle over the camera looking up where its tip's runout calibration found the nozzle's axis to be (a CameraOffset algorithm's Camera Position Offset), as the manual said and OpenPnP does. It went to the camera's own place, so every part on a nozzle whose axis is off over the camera was placed that far off (0.1 mm on the bench's left nozzle).
  • Issues & Solutions' precise nozzle offsets calibration shows the correction it made as soon as it ends, in a dialog: how far the nozzle's offsets moved, and the detected and previous offsets. The issue's own page shows them too when looked at again.
  • A nozzle tip that fails to calibrate while homing says so in a dialog, with the reason, instead of only in the status line. In a run, a tip that fails to calibrate pauses the run whatever the placements' Error Handling; Resume or Step measures it again, and the run goes on only once it is calibrated.
  • No crash capturing a location (a strip feeder's hole) on a setup page: a page's buttons now do their work once the click has been handled, so a page made again by what they do no longer goes from under the click.
  • Homing no longer stays busy for good (its button greyed until a restart) when a Machine Setup change is made while it finishes: a change to a camera, a head or an axis now waits until a camera task (a tip's runout measured as homing ends, a calibration) has ended, and the tip's runout is kept. Defaults, then Auto-Tune waits for a camera task too, instead of upsetting its pictures.
  • A strip feeder's Auto Setup Sets Z? (on to begin with): setting the Reference Hole Location's Z by hand (typed, or captured with the nozzle) turns it off, and Auto Setup then leaves the Z and Z Along Strip % as they are. The log says how big Auto Setup saw the sprocket holes, in mm, beside EIA-481's 1.5 mm.
  • A strip feeder with vision on a 2 mm pitch tape (0402s) looks at the tape on every pick, not every second one, unless its Extrapolation Distance says looks may be skipped.
  • Bottom vision looks for a part only where it can be (the part's own size plus the pick tolerance), not across the nozzle tip's whole Max Part Diameter: a small part (an 0402) is no longer boxed with whatever else shines round the tip. On a paused run, a Test Alignment of the part on the nozzle replaces the run's alignment.
  • A job's nozzle tip calibration shows each circle it finds on the bottom camera, as one from the Jog panel does.
  • Auto tool select follows a running job: the Jog panel chooses the nozzle or camera the job moves, so the footprint drawn on a camera turns with the part being placed. A job's messages and the feeder-loading window name parts by their names, not by long codes.
  • Cameras: a single damaged picture no longer makes jplacer close and reopen the camera (which showed as "could not start" over and over while the camera was running); settings are sent to a camera only when they change. A nozzle tip change or a tip calibration no longer rebuilds the whole machine setup (the pauses at each step of a run, and the Jog panel flickering).
  • A job's nozzle tip change no longer measures the new tip's runout twice: the second measurement, run beside the job, could fail or block the job's next move ("another move is under way") and leave a failure banner up after the job had calibrated the tip. The nozzle chooser on the Jog panel names the part on a nozzle.
  • Linked tables: what a link chooses on another tab is shown even if that tab had a search (the search is cleared) or a Show that left it out; before, it was not chosen at all.
  • The job's check before a run, and messages from a run (no feeder for a part, a part's height probe, bottom vision), the Select Feeder title and a stock lot's ledger, name parts by their names, not by a long code.
  • Board Nudge in the Job tab's Boards: when every part is out the same way after a fiducial check, turn it on over a part, jog the camera onto it and Apply: the board moves by what you jogged, and every placement with it.
  • Fiducials found more reliably: a small fiducial (a 1 mm one) is no longer missed for bare board or the silkscreen beside it (its label), which made a fiducial check fail or come out a millimetre or more off.
  • Importing a board again after deleting its parts from the library links its placements to the parts the import makes, instead of leaving them pointing at the deleted ones ("not in the library", Missing Part, and the part's columns empty). The same on New Revision. Removing a board's placements also removes the board's parts they used, so they cannot hold on to old library parts.

• The CPL and BOM import can also Fetch Dimensions from LCSC: each package with no body size or height is given them from its part's 3D model at LCSC. While footprints and dimensions are fetched, a window shows how far it has got and lists anything that went wrong, with Retry and Cancel (Packages' Fetch Missing Footprints uses it too). Parts and 3D models are kept, so each is fetched once.
  • A package's Footprint page says where its pads, body and height came from (LCSC, a KiCad file, a generator).
  • Importing a CPL and BOM remembers each file's columns as you set them (a "Val" column read as the part's Name, say): the next file with the same columns is read the same way, without saving a profile.
  • After an import, the dialog that follows (the parts to choose, or what to do with a board's existing placements) stays in front of the main window instead of going behind it on Linux.
  • The Job tab's Measure Board Z toggle only sets that setting (and saves it): it no longer applies the whole machine setup again, which could crash jplacer when pressed before homing. Press it again to take it back (it is no longer an Edit ▸ Undo step).

• Changing a setting only a job or a check uses (Machine Setup's Vision settings, the job processor's; the Job tab's Measure Board Z toggle) no longer makes the machine's panels again: the Jog panel no longer flickers.
  • The camera tab's target is now Hold Footprint Size, a toggle: while it is on, the footprint drawn over the picture is kept as big on the screen as it was when you pressed it, the picture zooming in or out as you go from placement to placement (Previous and Next), as far as the zoom goes; zoom by hand to change the size it holds. It no longer calibrates the camera, so it cannot start a calibration by mistake: that is Start Calibration on the camera's Advanced Calibration page (the gear).
  • The Job tab's Placements has Move Camera To Previous Placement Location (Next's arrow pointing back), left of Move Camera To Next Placement Location: the camera to the placement before the chosen one.
  • A submenu of a menu long enough to wrap into two columns (a table's Columns, its This View) can be reached: it opens over the second column, and moving the mouse across it used to hover that column's entry underneath and close it.
  • The Job tab's boards toolbar has a Measure Board Z toggle beside Fiducial Check: Machine Setup's Measure Board Z? (a fiducial check measures each board's height at its fiducials), turned on and off from there, lit while on.

• Importing a CPL and BOM no longer makes one part of different parts that share a name. EasyEDA's pick-and-place file names parts by their value, so every 100nF (0402 and 0603 alike) became one part, and the same for other values on more than one BOM line. Rows are now one part by their MPN, else their supplier's part number, else name, value and footprint together; parts sharing a name are told apart by footprint (100nF-C0402), and a library part is no longer taken by its name when the file's MPN, LCSC number or footprint says it is another. A board imported with 0.1.61 to 0.1.67 from such files should be imported again.

• A fiducial that is not found names its part (not its id), and says how near the roundest spot came to being taken (its score against Min. Symmetry). A failed fiducial check is written to the log too, not only shown.
  • Packages no longer have a Tape Specification: the tape a part comes on is its own Packaging. A push-pull feeder's Smart Clone now matches a template by the same package, or by a tape the parts share (the same width, pitch and type), not by that typed label.

• A package has a Height: its parts' height wherever a part has none of its own. The Parts table shows the package's greyed for those; typing a part's height gives it its own, emptying it takes the package's again. Parts keep the heights they have.
  • A placement whose library part was deleted shows what the files called its part (and not in the library), not a long id; pointing at it shows everything the files said of it.

• The Parts table shows each part's Supplier PN: where an LCSC number from an import is kept (and what its footprint is fetched by), and you can type one in. It was kept before, but shown only on the part's Library page.
  • The Job tab's Placements can show each placement's part's and package's columns (Part ▸ Value, Package ▸ Name and the rest, under Columns), and change them there: the change is the library part's or package's, so every placement of it shows it.

• Opening a job with a panel in it could close jplacer at once: a board or panel added to a panel (in the panel's definition) was saved without its file. They are saved with it now; a panel saved before, its boards naming no file, opens without them (the log says which), and is saved without them.

• The Job tab's Placements is the one place for a board: its toolbar has the board's Import Placements, Board's Parts, View Board and Revision, and a board's placements (their IDs, parts, sides, positions, types) are changed there for every board, wherever it is used. The Board and Panel tabs are gone: under the job's list is the chosen one's detail, a board's Placements or a panel's definition (its boards and fiducials).

• The head's Homing Fiducial Part lists only the library's parts ((none) until one is chosen), its list keeps up with parts added, renamed or deleted without leaving the head and coming back, and a deleted one shows as (none). A machine set up before the choice still uses (and shows) its part named FIDUCIAL-HOME.
  • No more Boards and Panels tabs: boards and panels are the job's. Choose one on the Job tab and the new Board (or Panel) tab beside its Placements is the board or panel itself: its placements, imports, revisions, parts and viewer, or a panel's children and fiducials. Make or add them with the Job tab's Add Board/Panel, which also offers Copy of the Chosen Board/Panel…. A board's or panel's Name, Width and Length are changed in the Job tab's table. Nothing made can drop out of sight any more, and your boards, panels and jobs open as before.
  • A feeder whose part was deleted from the library shows no part on the Feeders tab and its page, not a long ID; deleting parts names them, and says how many feeders hold them.

• The CSV/BOM import can read a part's Name (a column such as "Part Name" or "LibRef" is taken as Part ▸ Name): the part is called that, rows with one name are one part, and a library part of that name is found by it. With no name given, a part is named by its MPN, footprint and value together (CL10B104KB8NNNC-C0603-100n), so two parts are less likely to share a name.

• Footprints from LCSC: a package's footprint can be fetched by its LCSC part number (C14663), with no export from EasyEDA. Use the new LCSC button beside KiCad under the Footprint tab's Generate, Import LCSC Footprint… on its Footprints tab, Fetch Missing Footprints on the Packages toolbar (every package with no pads, by its parts' LCSC numbers), or the CSV/BOM import's Fetch Footprints from LCSC. Only the part number is sent; each answer is kept so a part is fetched once. Parts fetched for also get their description, MPN and height where they had none.
  • Start, Step and Stop are also in the toolbar at the top of the window, beside the machine's power and home buttons, so a job can be run from any tab.

• Board photos: a board can be photographed with the head camera, the pictures stitched into one photo square to the board, kept beside the board's file (every one until you delete it) and shown under the Board Viewer's drawing. Take one any time with the Job tab's new Photograph Board button (Stop stops it), or have the job take them as it starts (the bare board) and as it ends (Machine Setup > Job Processor > Board Photos). Pictures the machine put out of place are lined up by what they show, and how far out they were is said, so a photo is also a check on the camera's calibration.

• The CSV/BOM import has a Sides choice: Top and Bottom, Top Only or Bottom Only. Rows of the side left out are skipped and counted in What it makes; on a Merge, the board's placements on that side stay as they are.
  • Importing again fills in a library part's description, datasheet, MPN and supplier's part number only where it has none; what you have set is kept, and a different description in the files is noted in What it makes.
  • A part made by a CSV/BOM import (Create Missing Parts) now takes the files' description (the Parts table's Description), datasheet, MPN and supplier's part number, not only its value and height.
  • A head's Homing Fiducial Part (Machine Setup, beside Homing Fiducial) chooses the library part visual homing looks for the mark as, kept by the part itself so renaming it changes nothing; not chosen, the part named FIDUCIAL-HOME, as before.

• A feeder is known for good by a GUID, shown in the Feeders table's new ID column. Feeders brought in from an OpenPnP machine get one (OpenPnP's FDR… is not kept), as do those of an older feeders.json as it is read, any stock lot on one following it.
  • A package is known for good by a GUID, as a part is, and has a Name, shown wherever it is (a part's Package, the import) and changed in place on the Packages tab. New Package… asks for a name. A library of 0.1.56 or before is brought up to this as it opens, keeping every part's package.
  • A package's name learned from boards (its footprints' CAD Names) finds it in an import too, not only when choosing a part.
  • The library's Undo names parts and packages by their names ("Undo Delete Part R0603-10k"), and a vision setting's Assigned To lists parts by their names (they had shown GUIDs). Template images for vision are found by the part's and the package's names, as OpenPnP names them.
  • The table a feeder's Part or a part's Package drops has views too (Standard, All Fields, and more made with New View…), its buttons beside its filter. A table in a window of its own is a plain table: it offers no views and no fields to add or edit, only its columns to show and hide.

• Every table's things can have fields of your own: Add Field… in Columns or on a heading's right-click menu adds one (text, a number, a length, yes/no or a choice) to parts, packages, pads, placements, boards, panels, the job's boards, feeders or vision settings, and Job ▸ Job Fields… to jobs. A field is a column in every table of its kind, and Edit Fields… renames it, changes its type or deletes it. jplacer's own columns can be renamed, and those it can do without removed. The tables are described on a page of their own, Tables.
  • The Feeders and Vision tabs' tables have Columns too.
  • Importing a board from its CPL and BOM offers every field to fill, yours included: a placement's, a part's and its package's from each row, and a board's or the job's one value for the whole import (from a column, from what the file says about itself such as a KiCad board's revision, or typed in the window). New … Field… in a column's list makes a field named after the column. Parts and packages the import makes get their values; a library part keeps its own where it has one.
  • A KiCad board read for an import gives its footprints' own properties (LCSC, MPN, Datasheet…) as columns to fill fields with, and its title block for the board's and the job's fields.
  • Keep as extra is gone from the import: a column no field matches is ignored, or made a field of its own.
  • Every table has views: its layout (columns, order, widths, sort) kept under a name, switched with a button each beside Columns, or Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9. Each starts with Standard and All Fields (every column, always); New View… makes more, each with its own icon. A view can be renamed, given another icon, duplicated, moved (drag its button), locked (changes last until another view is shown) or made to keep its search. The Issues & Solutions table has Columns and views too.
  • A value typed, a tick or a choice in a row of several chosen goes into all of them, and Ctrl+V pastes cells copied from a table or a spreadsheet (one value into every row chosen; refused by one cell, nothing is pasted). Edit ▸ Undo takes back changes made in every table, not only the library's, one step a change.
  • Every table's Search can look in one field: lcsc: C15, or lcsc: for the rows with anything in it, the field's name completing as you type it (Tab takes it). What matched is marked in each cell, the count of rows found shows beside the box, and a row found only in a hidden column is marked and says which.
  • A library made by 0.1.55 opens as it is, and keeps the fields you add.

• A part has a Name, shown wherever the part is, and beside its ID on the Parts tab, where it is changed in place (unique in the library). Every part's ID is a GUID, made for it, so its name can be changed freely; a part starts with the name it came with (a board's name for it, OpenPnP's ID, or the name given it). OpenPnP's machine, boards, panels and jobs name parts by OpenPnP's ID, and are linked by Name.
  • The library has a new layout: start with a fresh one. An older library.db is refused, saying so; delete it (and OpenPnP's parts.xml and packages.xml in the same folder, to start without OpenPnP's parts), and the feeders, boards, panels and jobs made with it.
  • A job puts parts in order by their Name, as OpenPnP does by its IDs.
  • A library part always learns what a board calls it when they are linked (its Also Known As), so a part you renamed is still found by the next board.
  • Two library parts that answer to the same name (a 1 % and a 5 % resistor) are both offered when a board comes in, and neither is taken without asking.
  • jplacer keeps everything of its own in JSON files: jobs are .jpjob and panels .jppanel (as boards are .jpboard), and the feeders, vision settings and what feeders keep on the machine are JSON files in the configuration folder. OpenPnP's jobs, boards and panels still open as they are; saved, each is written beside OpenPnP's file as jplacer's, and OpenPnP's is left as it was. Start the feeders afresh (import an OpenPnP machine, or set them up again); OpenPnP's vision settings are read until jplacer has its own.
  • Saving the machine, a board or any of jplacer's files writes it whole or not at all, so a crash or a full disk part way never leaves a half-written file. Before, the machine's set-up and a board could be cut short.
  • An older OpenPnP job opened is no longer copied to a backup beside it: jplacer saves its own file and leaves OpenPnP's alone.
  • jplacer no longer counts OpenPnP's default parts and packages as taken in again at every start (which saved the configuration each time for nothing).
  • A blinds feeder's Push Z Offset is used: its cover was always pushed at the default 0.25 mm, whatever it was set to.
  • An OpenPnP machine saved by an older OpenPnP brings its feeders' retry count in as their feed retries, as OpenPnP does (they had come in as 3 feed and 3 pick retries).

• The Parts table has more columns to show with Columns (hidden until chosen): Packaging, Suppliers, Manufacturer, Stock and Datasheet. A part with several shows how many and the first ("(2) Cut tape 8/4"); point at the cell for all of them. Search finds a part by any of them (a supplier's SKU, say). The feeder Part list's table has them too.
  • A column shown again comes back as wide as the others, not as a sliver.
  • Help ▸ About jplacer shows the Jaytek logo above jplacer's version, copyright, licence and link, as jayecu Studio's About box does, and credits OpenPnP, whose icons, translations, defaults and illustrations jplacer carries.
  • The AppImage now carries jplacer's licence, a notice of what comes from OpenPnP and elsewhere, and the licences of OpenCV and nanosvg, which are built in.

• A feeder takes its part's packaging: under Part, Packaging lists the ways the part comes (its Packagings on the Library tab), and choosing one puts its rotation, tape width and pitch into the feeder's settings (a strip feeder's Rotation In Tape, Tape Width and Part Pitch, and the like on other kinds). Loading a part takes its only packaging, or the one last chosen for it, by itself.
  • Part is at the top of every feeder's page (the Photon and heap feeders had it further down).
  • A packaging's tape width and pitch keep their decimals (2.5 mm was read back as 2).
  • The tables on the Job, Boards, Panels, Parts and Packages tabs have a Columns icon at the end of their toolbars: tick the columns to show, untick those to hide. Each table keeps its own choice, with its column order, widths and sort.
  • A feeder's Part drops the Parts tab's own table to choose from, every column of it: sort, move and widen its columns there, and choose them with its Columns icon; it keeps its layout apart from the Parts tab's. The box becomes a filter line (its ✕ empties it), with the Parts tab's Show beside it (All, Used by open boards, each open board). The Parts tab's Package (the Packages tab's table), a feeder bank slot's part and a panel fiducial's Part choose the same way.
  • Tables no longer draw a row scrolled part way up over their column titles.
  • jplacer opens on the tabs you left in front. With a panel closed (Job, Panels), it always opened on the Console tab.
  • Each camera's right-click menu has Reticle Style…: the colour and line thickness of its reticle (the cross, grid, ruler, circle or square) and of a footprint drawn over the picture, colours from the colour chooser, kept with the camera. Shown as you change them.

• A feeder's Part is chosen from a list you can search. Type to narrow it: lq finds every LQFP, 0603 100n finds 100 nF parts in 0603 (a value however written: 100n finds 0.1u), and cap, res, ind, led and fid find parts by how their footprints are named. Each part shows its value, package and the open boards that use it. All, In the Job and each open board choose where to look; a feeder starts on In the Job, with the parts no feeder holds yet first. The Parts tab's Package and a panel fiducial's Part are searched the same way.

• Changing many placements or boards at once (Set Enabled, Set Type, Set Side, Set Error Handling, Set Placed, a panel's fiducials' side) no longer freezes jplacer: the change is saved and shown once, not once for every placement chosen.

• Moving the camera to a place (Machine Setup's Move Camera, the Feeders tab's) takes its Z there too, as OpenPnP does: a camera's virtual Z then says the height it looks at, and the reticle and footprint are drawn to scale at that height. Before, the camera stayed at safe Z.
• The Jog panel's Z park on a camera takes its Z back up to safe Z; it did nothing for a camera's virtual Z.

• A camera looking up draws its reticle and the footprint at the height of what a nozzle over it holds (the part's underside), so with a calibration at two heights the footprint still fits a part raised above the camera's Z.
  • Bottom vision measures a part at the camera's scale at the camera's own Z, where it brings the part's underside, even when the camera was calibrated at other heights.
  • The Console's Force Upper Case and the controller it sends to, and the Log tab's Search, Log Level and System Output, are kept from one run to the next, as the log levels and G-code already were.

• Issues & Solutions' precise nozzle offsets have a Test Object Z box: the test object's height can be typed in, as well as captured with the nozzle touching it.
  • Tooltips come up when the pointer rests, without needing a small nudge of the mouse first.

• The Jog panel has Backlash Compensation under the pad: unticked, no axis is compensated, for every move, so teaching a tip changer's slots no longer carries the nozzle past its place into a wall. It is ticked each time jplacer starts. With Backlash Off Below Safe Z (the Safety tab, on to begin with) it is unticked by itself while the head is below safe Z, and ticked again once it is back up. An axis's Backlash Compensation tab says whether compensation is on now and, when it is off, why (unticked on the Jog panel, the head below safe Z, or backlash being calibrated), so a method set there that is not being used is explained.
  • A Machine Setup or Feeders tab wider than its pane now scrolls sideways, with a bar along the bottom (or the wheel with Shift held), as a long one scrolls down; its notes wrap to the pane's width. On a narrow window a nozzle tip's Backlash? column and step buttons can be reached.

• Fixed: on a nozzle tip's Tool Changer tab, a step's Move Nozzle and Capture took the step's coordinates one place along (its X as Y, its Y as Z), because the row starts with Kind. Move Nozzle sent the nozzle to the wrong place, and a Z out of range was refused by the soft limits; Capture would have written into the wrong columns. They now take the step's X, Y, Z and Rotation.
  • A nozzle tip's loading and unloading moves no longer have Position Tool (Without Safe Z): Move Nozzle goes as the step is set, by way of safe Z only with Safe Z? ticked, and backlash compensated only with Backlash?.

• A nozzle tip's loading and unloading steps are all on the tip's Tool Changer tab, no longer a page each in the tree. Each move has Safe Z? (up, across, then down; otherwise straight there) and Backlash? (compensated like every other move; otherwise without going past the place and back, which could push the tip into a slot's wall). Moves saved before keep how they ran: the first by way of safe Z, the rest straight, none compensated. The first move must go by way of safe Z, or the tip shows a problem. Unloading as loading backwards undoes each move the way it went, and its steps are listed on the same tab.
  • Each move's place buttons move as the step does, and Position Tool (Without Safe Z) is back on them, so the nozzle can be taken from one step to the next as the change goes.

• Parts and packages now live only in the library: a board's placements point at library parts, and boards no longer keep parts, packages or copies of their own. Create Missing Parts adds the parts (and packages) the library lacks when you take the import (Merge, Replace or New Revision), not while you're only looking at it. A board saved before is converted as it opens: its own parts and packages go into the library, and the log says how many.
  • The Parts and Packages tabs list the library; the Source icon shows a board for anything an open board uses, and Show picks All, Used by open boards, or one board. The part picker's Make It the Board's Own, and the Board's Parts window's Take the Library's and Give the Library the Board's, are gone with the board copies.

• Every table's columns can be moved: drag a heading sideways and the table shows how it will look as you drag, letting go keeps it and Escape puts it back. Every table now remembers its columns' order, widths and sort, including after a restart, and right-click on a heading offers Reset Columns.
  • The Parts and Packages tabs' Source is the first column, an icon: books for the library, a board for an open board (its name in the tooltip).
  • Show beside Search on the Parts and Packages tabs no longer starts empty when no job is open; it starts on All.

• The Parts and Packages tabs list every open board's parts and packages under the library's, so you can see what a board actually carries. A board's rows have the board icon and a tinted Source (the board's name), and Status says Own, Matched, Library changed or To be chosen. Show beside Search lists all, the library's, the boards', or one board's. A board's own part or package is edited there (the board then asks to be saved), right-click Add to Library copies it into the library, and Update from Library refreshes a board's copy the library has changed.
  • A board's own parts keep their value, identifiers and packaging when the board is saved; before, only what OpenPnP's part file holds was kept, and their Value column was empty.

• The Machine tab is gone: everything on it is on Machine Setup's pages. A controller's page now also shows its State (Idle, Run, Alarm…, or not connected), kept up to date.
